full_judgment:
Sheikh Hassan Arif J: Since the core principles of law raised and to be settled in the aforesaid customs appeals are similar, namely the maintain-ability of the said appeals before the High Court Division, they have been taken up together for hearing and are now being disposed of by this single judgment.

2. In Customs Appeal No. 17 of 2008, the appellant Md Shahadat Hossain, proprietor of M/s Shahadat Hossain, Seuzgari, Bogra, was proceeded against for alleged importation of excess wheat’s from India through Hilli Station, Dinajpur under Bill of Entry No. 4667 dated 11-6-2005 and Bill of Entry No. 48/72 dated 21-6-2005, EXP No. 2292 dated 10-6-2005 being covered under Letter of Credit No. 1945-05-01-0272 dated 9-6-2005. Accordingly, the appellant was found liable for punishment for violation of the provisions under sections 16 and 32 of the Customs Act, 1969 and section 3(1) of the Import and Export Control Act, 1950 and thereby found to have committed offence under sections 156(1), 9(1) and 14 of the Customs Act, 1969 and was imposed a penalty of Taka 10 lac by the Commissioner of Customs, Rajshahi vide Adjudication Order dated 5-4-2006 as communicated vide Nothi No. 5-CUS-8(92) Aniom/Hilli/05/2609(6) dated 24-4-2006. Being aggrieved by this Adjudication Order, the appellant-importer preferred an appeal before the Customs, Excise and Vat Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka (respondent No. 2) (hereinafter called "the Tribunal") under section 196A of the Customs Act, 1969 ("the said Act"). However, since the appellant did not, or failed to, deposit 50% of the penalty imposed in compliance with the provisions of section 194 of the said Act, his Appeal was rejected by the Tribunal as being not maintainable vide impugned order dated 20-2-2008 as communicated by Nothi No. CEVT/CASE(Cus)- 287/2006/152(1-2) dated 25-2-2008. As against this order, the Appellant has preferred the instant Appeal before the High Court Division under section 196D of the said Act.

3. In Customs Appeal No. 22 of 2007, the appellant (Dhaka Beijing Dyeing and Weaving Industries Ltd, Banani, Dhaka) imported 23,850 Kg. threads and released them after payment of duties through Bill of Entry No. 2030 dated 12-2-2004. According to the appellant-importer, while the said goods were being taken to its industry at DEPZ, Savar by three trucks under Risk Bond, 7,850 Kg of threads there from were snatched by miscreants on the way on 19-2-2004. However, this contention of the appellant was not believed by the customs authority, who proceeded against the appellant for violation of the provisions under sections 86 and 87 of the said Act and thus found it responsible for the removal of the said threads and directed it to pay the duties for an amount of Taka 4,62,599 on the said removed goods and to pay a penalty of Taka 30,000 under Clauses-1, 51 and 90 of the Table under section 156(1) of the said Act vide order No. 58/05 dated 11-5-2005 passed by the Commissioner, Customs Bond Commissionerate, Shegunbagicha, Dhaka. Being aggrieved by this order, the appellant preferred an Appeal before the Tribunal under section 196A of the said Act. However, the Tribunal dismissed the same for default vide order dated 23-1-2007 as no body was found present on behalf of the appellant when the said Appeal was taken up, or called up, by the Tribunal for hearing. The appellant then filed an application for restoration (though the Tribunal termed it as 'review application') of the said Appeal, whereupon the Tribunal, vide impugned order dated 6-6-2007, rejected the same. The appellant, thereafter, has preferred the instant Appeal before the High Court Division under section 196D of the said Act against the said order dated 6-6-2007 passed by the Tribunal. 4. In Customs Appeal No. 25 of 2008, the Appellant, Mr Salahuddin Ahmed, proprietor of M/s Friends International, Bangshal Road (1st Floor), Dhaka-1100, imported some 'PVC Floor Covering' from India under PSI Scheme being covered by LC No. 1622 -06-01-0065 dated 18-4-2007. Though the total invoice value of the said goods was declared as USD 11,380.50 (CNF), the concerned PSI Agent certified the CRF value of the same as US$ 11,456.72 vide CRF No. SG/07/554390 dated 12-6-2007. However, the Customs Authority refused to accept the said CRF value and determined its value as USD 16,285.19 (USD .79 per Kg). The appellant then released the said goods through BIE No. C 11138 dated 27-6- 2007 after payment of duties as per the value determined by the customs authority upon furnishing bank guarantee for the excess duty imposed and filed a Complaint before the Review Committee as constituted under section 193C of the said Act read with Rule 23 of the Pre Shipment Inspection Rules, 2002 for release of the said bank guarantee. The Review Committee then, upon hearing the parties, rejected the said Complaint by its decision as communicated vide Nathi No. 5- Cus/8/(l15) Pre-Shipl Review/2007/1503(6) dated 26-6-2007. As against this decision of the Review Committee, the appellant preferred an Appeal before the Tribunal under section 193C(2) [though the Appellant mentioned 'section 196A'] of the said Act, whereupon the Tribunal, after hearing the parties, dismissed the same upon affirming the decision of the Review Committee vide impugned order dated 12-3-2008 as communicated vide Nothi No. CEVT/case (Cus)-613/ 2007/205(1-5) dated 17-3-2008. Being aggrieved by this order of the Tribunal, the appellant has preferred the instant Appeal before the High Court Division under section 1960 of the said Act.

5. Since section 1960 of the said Act has made specific mention of "an order under section 196B", the common question in the aforesaid three appeals stemming from three different situations is whether the above impugned orders as passed by the Tribunal are orders passed under section 196B of the said Act, thereby entitling the appellants to prefer the aforesaid appeals before the High Court Division against the same under section 1960 of the said Act. Considering the importance of the legal issues involved and divergence of opinion prevailing at the Bar on the same, we have requested Mr Mahmudul Islam and Mr AF Hassan Ariff, learned senior advocates, to assist this Court as Amicus Curiae. Accordingly, the said learned advocates have made their valuable submissions before this Court at length. We have also heard Mr AM Aminuddin, learned advocate, as intervener. At the same time Mr Munshi Moniruzzaman with Mr Akhtar Farhad Zaman, Mr Shamsuddin Babul with Mr Kanailal Shah, and Mr Mohammad Jahirul Islam, learned advocates and Mr Goutam Kumar Roy, Md Muniruzzaman, learned DAGs have assisted us by putting forward their submissions and suggestions on the issues involved.

6. As regards the situation in Customs Appeal No. 17 of 2008, Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned advocate, submits that the order passed by the Tribunal rejecting the Appeal as being not maintainable for non deposit of 50% of the duty demanded or of the penalty imposed etc. is not an order under section 196B of the said Act. According to him since the appeal could not even cross the threshold of deposit imposed by section 194 of the said Act, the appeal itself was not in form and, as such, the order of the Tribunal rejecting the same cannot be regarded as an order passed under section 196B thereby entitling the appellant to prefer an appeal against such order(s) before this Court under section 1960 of the said Act. This view of Mr Mahmudul Islam is also supported by Mr Aminuddin, learned advocate and Mr Moniruzzaman, learned DAG.

7. In respect of the situation in Customs Appeal No. 22 of2007, Mr Islam submits that the order dismissing an appeal for default or an order rejecting an application for restoration of the said appeal should be regarded to have been passed by the Tribunal as an adjudicating entity as the Tribunal is already in seisin of the appeal preferred before it and, as such, the said order should be deemed to be an order as against which appeal should be held to be maintainable before the High Court Division under section 196D of the said Act. Mr Islam further argues that since the High Court Division in one writ petition (Writ Petition No. 3859 of 2008) has already held that the Tribunal cannot pass an order dismissing the appeal for default, the order passed by the Tribunal dismissing an appeal for default is an order without jurisdiction and, as such, appeal should lie against the same before the High Court Division under section 196D of the said Act. Mr Aminuddin and Mr Moniruzzaman, however, have expressed the opposite view in that since the order dismissing the appeal for default or the order rejecting application for restoration of the said appeal is not an order under section 196B of the said Act, the same is not amenable to appeal before the High Court Division. According to them, the Tribunal can only pass four categories of orders as specifically mentioned in sub-section (1) of section 196B once the said appeal is in form. According to them, since these four types of orders are specifically contemplated in section 196B, the order passed by the Tribunal dismissing the appeal for default or any other order not being one of the said four categories should not be regarded as an order passed under section 196B and, as such, no appeal should lie to the High Court Division against such order(s).

8. As regards the situation in Customs Appeal No. 25 of 2007, Mr Islam submits that since the order passed by the Tribunal in such a situation is an order under sub-section (3) of section 193C regarding determination of the price of the goods under PSI Scheme for the purpose of final assessment, the same is not an order under section 196B and, as such, appeal should not lie against it before the High Court Division under section 196D. This view is, however, supported by Mr Aminuddin, learned advocate and Mr Moniruzzaman, learned DAG.

9. Mr AF Hassan Ariff, learned advocate Nsi and the other Amicus Curiae, has, however, argued from an entirely different angle giving particular emphasis on the words-"pass such orders thereon as it thinks fit as occurring in sub-section (1) of section 196B. Mr Ariff submits that these words in section 196B (1) have gave the dimension of the orders, as may be passed by the Tribunal under section 196B, a very wide spectrum. According to him, any order giving final determination of the appeal before the Tribunal should come within the perview of the order(s) under section 196B. Mr Ariff argues that the Legislature has deliberately used those words by putting a coma (,) after them, thereby separating them from the other four categories of orders mentioned thereafter in sub-section (1) of section 196B. Thus, he continues, any order terminating the very appeal itself before the Tribunal should be regarded as an order passed under section 196B, thereby making it amenable to appeal before the High Court Division under section 196D. As regards the appeals before the Tribunal from the decisions of the Review Committee, Mr Ariff points out that he has found four sources of appeals to the Tribunal, viz, two sources as mentioned under section 196A(1)(a) and (b), one source mentioned under section 193C(2) and another mentioned under Rule-16 of the Bonded Ware House Rules-2008. According to him, whatever may be the sources of such appeals before the Tribunal, whenever the Tribunal passes any order giving finality to such appeals in what-so-ever manner, such order should be regarded as an order passed under section 196B and, as such, the same should be held to be amenable to appeal before the High Court Division under section 196D. He further points out that since the order to be passed by the Tribunal has to be an order which will terminate the very appeal, each and every order of the Tribunal in the course of disposal of such appeal will not be amenable to appeal before the High Court Division as those orders will not terminate the appeal itself. Thus, he submits, the test should be that the order which terminates the appeal is only amenable to further appeal before the High Court Division as the same will be art order under section 196B of the said Act.

10. Considered the submissions of the learned advocates, perused the petitions of Appeals, impugned orders and other materials on record. The legal question involved in the afore-said Appeals touches upon the jurisdiction of the High Court Division as conferred under section 196D of the said Act to entertain a further appeal against order(s) passed by the Tribunal. For better understanding of the words used in conferring such jurisdiction, section 196D is quoted below:

"196D. Appeal to the High Court Division:—The Commissioner of Customs or the other party may, within ninety days of the date upon which he is served with notice of An order under section 196B, by an application prefer an appeal to the High Court Division against such order".

<u>11. The words used in the above section are very much important for the purpose of interpretation of the same and to determine the scope of the said special appellate jurisdiction of the High Court Division. While interpreting those words and other relevant provisions of the said Act, we have to keep in mind some basic presumptions as widely accepted by the superior Courts in the construction of statutes. As for examples, there is always a strong presumption against ousting the established jurisdiction of the Courts, in particular the superior Courts. When the Legislature confers a special or additional jurisdiction on a recognized Court without mentioning the manner in which it has to be exercised, all the rules of procedures that apply to its ordinary jurisdiction will be attracted in regard to the said special or additional jurisdiction [See Mahmudul Islam, Interpretation of Statutes and Documents, Mallick Brothers (2009) P-60]. This presumption draws its support from various decisions of the superior Courts of this sub-continent [e.g. Mohammed Zulfigar vs Abul Kalam, 42 DLR (AD) 83, Superintendent and Legal Remembrance vs Zuhed Ali, 26 DLR (AD) 1, Zamil Hoque vs Bangladesh 34 DLR (AD) 125 and Md Ismail vs State, PLD 1969 (SC) 241]. However, this presumption has to be applied inconformity with the other similarly strong presumption against creating new and enlarging existing jurisdiction. This presumption is that when the law has conferred jurisdiction expressly, no amount of consent by the parties can invest the Court with jurisdiction which is not given by law [See Mahmudul Hoque vs Shamsul Alam, 36 DLR (AD) 171].</u>

<u>12. Jurisdiction of Courts, be it appellate or other, cannot be conferred by consent of the parties or by bonafide act of the parties. It is a creature of statute. Therefore, appeal from any decisions or orders of any tribunal must be given by express enactment. When by special law a particular jurisdiction is conferred on a regular Court or superior Court and the statute maintains silence about the manner in which such jurisdiction is to be exercised, then all rules of procedure that apply to the ordinary jurisdiction of the said Court will be attracted and that Court or superior Court is to be deemed to posses, as inherent in its jurisdiction, all such powers as are necessary to the right and undo the wrong in the course of administration of justice on the principle that when a law gives a person anything it gives that without which it cannot exist. In a recent case decided by this Bench [Customs Appeal No. 86 of 2008], this Court has relied on the last mentioned principle of interpretation and held that although section 196D of the Customs Act, 1969 was silent about the power of the High Court Division to send the Appeal back to the lower authority on remand, the High Court Division possessed such powers in the absence of any contrary expression in section 196D. "(quande lex aliquid alicui concedit concedera videtorid sine quores ispsa essenon polest)",</u>

<u>13. Section 196D provides that an appeal may be preferred before the High Court Division either by the Commissioner of Customs or by the other party within ninety days of the date upon which he is served with notice of an order under section 196B. The plain reading of the said section leads us to understand that to prefer an appeal or to maintain an appeal before the High Court Division, the impugned order has to be an order passed by the Tribunal under section 196B of the said Act. Thus, the statute, namely the Customs Act, 1969, has conferred a special appellate jurisdiction on the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh only against such order passed by the Tribunal which is "an order under section 196B". Therefore, since the words "an order under section .196B"have been expressly mentioned in section 196D, we may safely hold that the statute is not silent in specifying the appellate jurisdiction which has been conferred on the High Court Division. Here, the High Court Division will exercise its appellate jurisdiction not as a general appellate forum like it exercises under the Code of Civil Procedure, but as a special appellate forum against some orders passed by the Tribunal under section 196B.</u>

14. Appeals to the Tribunal are directed from several roots. We have so far found four such roots (thanks to Mr Ariff), viz. two roots as mentioned under Clauses (a) and (b) of section 196A(I), one mentioned under sub-section (2) of section 193C and the other under Rule 16 of the Bonded Ware House Rules, 2008. Whatever may be the said roots or sources of appeal to the Tribunal, the said Act has envisaged two manners in which such appeals are to be disposed of by the Tribunal. Sub-section (3) of section 193C has provided for one such manner of disposal of appeals preferred against the decision of the Review Committee in connection with the determination of price of goods imported under PSI Scheme. In this category of appeals, the Tribunal is empowered to pass such order as it thinks fit including fixing the price of the said goods for the purpose of final assessment. Thus, the orders which may be passed by the Tribunal in this category of appeals are not limited, but one of them is fixing the price of the goods imported under PSI Scheme for the purpose of final assessment fixing. However, the manner of disposal of other appeals is provided under sub-section (1) of section 196B, which additionally enunciates the powers and functions of the Tribunal in disposing of such appeals. Sub-section (1) of section 1968 reads as follows:

"196B. Order of Appellate Tribunal.-(l) The Appellate Tribunal may, after giving the parties to the appeal, an opportunity of being heard, pass such orders thereon as it thinks fit confirming modifying or annulling the decision or order or may refer the case back to the authority which passed such decision or order with such directions as the Appellate Tribunal may think fitfor a fresh adjudication or decision, as the case may be, after taking additional evidence, if necessary. 	.

(2) 	.

(3) 	.

(4) 	.

15. It appears from the above provision that the jurisdiction and the manner of exercise of such jurisdiction of the Tribunal have been enumerated in specific terms. Since Mr Ariff has given special emphasis on the use of punctuation 'Coma (,)' after the words "as it thinks fit" in sub-section (1) of section 196B, it deserves examination by this Court.

16. English Courts expressed doubt as to the importance of punctuation for the purpose of construction of Statutes [See IRC vs Hinchy (1960) 1 All ER 505, Director of Public Prosecution vs Schildkmp (1969) 3 All ER 1940]. The situation in Indian cases is also not that much different. Lord Bobhouse in a Privy Council case observed: "It is an error to rely on punctuation in construing Acts of the Legislature" [Moharani of Burdwan vs Krishna Kamini Dashi], ILR 14 Cal-365, P-372 (PC). However, in some modern cases, it would appear that judges of the superior courts relied upon the punctuation carefully used in the statutes for reaching conclusion as to the proper interpretation of the same. As for example, where Section 27 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 provides 'whoever manufactures for sale, sells, stocks or exhibits for sale or distributes' a drug without a license is liable for punishment, the Supreme Court of India pointed out the presence of Coma (,) after the words 'manufactures for sale' and 'sells' and absence of any Coma after the word 'stocks' to hold that mere stocking is not an offence. In this regard, the following expression of BK Mukherjea, J in Aswini Kumar Ghose vs Arobinda Bose [AIR 1952 SC 369, P-383] is pertinent to be mentioned here:

"Punctuation is after all a minor element in the construction of a statute, and very little attention is paid to it by English Courts-It seems, however, that in the vellum copies printed since 1850, there are some cases of punctuation, and when they occur they can be looked upon as a sort of contamporania exposition- When a statute is carefully punctuated and there is doubt about its meaning, a weight should undoubtedly be given to punctuation-I need not deny that punctuation may have its uses in some cases, but it cannot certainly be regarded as a controlling element and cannot be allowed to control the plain meaning of a text."

[Quoted from Justice GP Singh, Principles of Statutory Interpretation, 11th Edition 2008,Wadhwa and Nagpur, PP 168-170]

17. The essence, as' may be drawn from above, is that though punctuation is not very important, yet, when used carefully by the Legislature, it may sometimes be taken into consideration to give a proper interpretation of a particular statute.

<u>18. We have carefully examined the words used in sub-section (1) of Section 196B as well as the Coma (,) used after the words "as it thinks fit". It appears that similar words and expressions have been used in Section 193A of the said Act while specifying, in the same way, the manner of disposal of appeals by the Commissioner of Appeal. Sub-section (3) of Section 193A contains similar expressions "pass such order as he thinks fit confirming, modifying or annulling the decision or order appealed against" however, no Coma (,) has been used after the words 'as he thinks fit'. Thus, it is apparent that though the Legislature used similar expressions with similar words in two sections, namely sub-section (3) of Section 193A and sub-section (1) of Section 196B under the same Chapter XIX of the said Act, punctuation 'Coma (,), has not been used in both the provisions. This cursory use 'Coma' leads us to hold that the punctuation 'Coma' has not been used by the Legislature carefully is sub-section (1) of Section 196B and, as such, should not be given any importance or interpreted as separating the words "pass such orders as it (or he) thinks fit" from the words "confirming, modifying or annulling”, thereby making them separate category or categories from the four categories of orders, namely confirming, modifying or annulling or sending the case back on remand, as mentioned thereafter. Thus, we are of the view that the use of the same 'Coma' in Section 196B (1) after the words "as it thinks fit" is not a careful use of the same to give any separate meaning and, as such, it does not carry any importance.</u>

<u>19. The plain reading of the provisions under sub-section (1) of Section 196B as well as sub-section (3) of Section 193A will lead us only to one conclusion that when the Legislature used the words "pass such order as he thinks tit" in sub-section (3) of Section 193A or "as it thinks fit" in sub-section (1) of Section 196B, it meant to express the same meaning which is that the Tribunal may pass such orders in disposing of the Appeal as it thinks fit and those orders are four categories of orders which are as follows:-</u>

<u>1) Confirming the decision or order appealed against,</u>

<u>2) Modifying the decision or order appealed against,</u>

<u>3) Annulling the decision or order appealed against, or</u>

4) Referring the case back to the authority which passed such decision or order with such directions as the Tribunal may think fit

20. Apart from the above four categories of orders, the Tribunal, in an appeal preferred before it, might have to pass so many other orders in the process of disposal of such appeal. But those orders will not be orders under Section 196B.

21. When an appeal is preferred before the Tribunal, either under the categories mentioned in Clauses (a) and (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 196A or under sub-section (2) of Section 193C or under Rule 16 of Bonded Ware House Licensing Rules, 2008 or under any other provisions, the Tribunal will have to dispose of the same in accordance with the provisions of the said Act or Rules framed (or to be framed) under sub-section (4) of Section 196A. However, to be an appeal before the Tribunal, the appellant must cross the hurdle of Section 194, namely that it will have to deposit 50% of the duty demanded or penalty imposed or both, as the case may be, before consideration of such appeal by the Tribunal. Unless this 50% deposit is made, or requirement of such deposit is dispensed with by the Tribunal in view of the sec-and proviso to sub-Section (1) of Section 1947the appeal cannot be considered by the Tribunal as the same is not a competent appeal. In other words, the appeal is not in form and, as such, the order of the Tribunal rejecting the same as being not maintainable, though terminates the very appeal, does not make it an order passed under Section 196B. To be an order as specified under Section 196B, the appeal has to be a competent one and regular one. Unless the deposit as required under Section 194 of the said Act is made or dispensed with before consideration of the same, it will not be a competent appeal. Consequently, the question of passing any order on the same under Section 196B of the said Act does not arise. If we hold otherwise, it will be contrary to the binding decision of our Appellate Division in Bombay Sweets Company Ltd vs President, Appellate Tribunal, V ADC (2008) 478. Without such deposit, since the appeal is not a competent appeal or appeal in form, the same cannot be considered by the Tribunal on merit. Thus, any order rejecting the said appeal as not maintainable will not be an order passed on a competent appeal and, as such any such order cannot be an order under Section 196B.

<u>22. Again, since the Tribunal may only pass four categories of orders under Section 196B and cannot pass any other order once the appeal is a competent one in view of Section 194 of the said Act, the order dismissing the said appeal for default on account of the absence of the appellant or his representative will be an order without jurisdiction as has already been held by this Court in Writ Petition No. 3859 of 2008 (Selim Mohammad vs The Appellate Tribunal and others). Thus, such order dismissing the said appeal for- default cannot be an order under Section 196B, though it is an order without jurisdiction. When the Legislature expressly mentioned the categories of orders to be appealed against before the High Court Division other orders, without or within jurisdiction, cannot be held to be amenable to appeal to the High Court Division. For the same reason, the order rejecting an application for restoring an appeal, which has already been dismissed for default, is also not an order which falls under the said four categories of orders under Section 196B and, as such, appeal against the same will also not lie before the High Court Division.</u>

23. It has been contended from the Bar that in some Customs Appeals, this Court interfered in recent past when the Tribunal rejected the appeal before it for the said non-deposit without considering the appellants application for dispensing with such requirement on the ground of hardship. On such impugned orders, this Court allowed the appeal and the case was sent back on remand to the Tribunal for hearing and disposal on remit of the same upon dispensing with the requirement of such deposit by the appellant. We have come across one of such decisions of this Court in Customs Appeal No. 37 of 2007 in which one of us was party. It appears from the said decision that the issue of maintainability of the very appeal was not raised therein and, accordingly, this Court did not also go into the said issue. Thus, the said decision cannot be regarded as a precedent for deter-mining the issues raised in the instant Appeals as regards the maintainability of appeal before the High Court Division.

24. Apart from above, we have also considered the words used in sub-section (3) of Section 193C providing the manner of disposal of appeals by the Tribunal preferred against the decisions of the Review Committee for the determination of the price of goods imported under PSI Scheme. It appears that the statute has contemplated a bit different manner for the same Tribunal to dispose of the said appeals. However, this slightly different manner of disposal of an appeal does not exclude it from the scope of orders under sub-section (1) of Section 196B if, upon disposal of the same on merit, the Tribunal passes one of the four categories of orders specified under sub-section (1) of Section 196B. We do not see any reason as to why such orders should also not be amenable to appeal before the High Court Division under Section 196D. Once the result of such disposal is one of the said four categories mentioned under sub-section (1) of Section 196B, it will become an order of the Tribunal passed under Section 196B and thus will entitle the Commissioner of Customs or other party to prefer appeal before the High Court Division under Section 196D. Thus, we hold that the Customs Appeal No. 25 of 2008, being an Appeal against an order passed by the Tribunal confirming the decision of the Review Committee, is maintainable under Section 196D of the said Act.

25. Since Customs Appeal No. 25 of 2008 is maintainable, we are to dispose of the same on merit. Mr. Jahirul Islam, learned advocate for the Appellant, submits that the Customs Authority arbitrarily refused to accept the CRF value in violation of the mandatory provisions of law. He further submits that if the value certified by the PSI agent is not acceptable to the Customs Authority, the provisions under Valuation Rules, 2000 will apply, which prescribes several stages for determination of the value of the goods in question. However, he argues, the Customs Authority did not at all follow those stages and put a higher value on the said goods. Mr Protikar Chakma, learned AAG, on the other hand, supports the higher value as imposed by the Customs Authority.

26. We have gone through the impugned order dated 12-3-2008 passed by the Tribunal as well as the decision of the Review Committee as communicated by file dated 26-9-2007. From both the decisions of the Review Committee as well as the impugned order passed by the Tribunal, we do not find anything on record that either the Review Committee or the Tribunal has ever taken recourse to the Valuation Rules, 2000and the stages for determination of valuation as mentioned therein under Rules 3,4,5,6,7 and 9 while imposing a higher value on the goods in question upon rejecting the CRF value as certified by the concerned PSI Agent. On the other hand, it appears from the decision of the Review Committee that the representative of the concerned PSI agent has placed the sale agreement, price justification letter obtained from the exporter/supplier. However, there is nothing on record that the same have been taken into consideration. The decision and orders of the lower authorities also do not reveal any cogent reason as to why the values as mentioned in the sale agreement and the price justification letter have been rejected. This attitude of the lower authorities, on the contrary, reflects the arbitrariness on their part. Thus, the decision of the Review Committee and the impugned order passed by the Tribunal cannot sustain in the eye of law. Regards being held to the above reasons, we find merit in the appeal. Accordingly, the Customs Appeal No. 25 of 2008 is allowed without any order as to costs. Thus, the decision and order of the lower authorities in imposing and/or affirming the higher value on the goods in question are set aside. In the result, the CRF value stands.

<u>27. With the above discussions of law and facts, the questions as raised in the aforesaid appeals are answered in the following terms:</u>

<u>1)	An order of the Tribunal rejecting an appeal as being not maintainable for non-deposit of 50% of the duty demanded or penalty imposed in accordance with the provisions of Section 194 of the said Act is not an order' under Section 196B of the said Act. Accordingly, no appeal against such orders shall lie before the High Court Division under Section 1960 of the said Act. Thus, the Customs Appeal No. 17 of 2008 is dismissed as being not maintainable.</u>

<u>2)	The order of the Tribunal dismissing the appeal before it for default or the order rejecting an application for restoration of the said Appeal is not an order under Section 196B of the said Act. Accordingly, no appeal against such order(s) shall lie before the High Court Division under Section 1960 of the said Act. Thus, the Customs Appeal No.22 of 2007 is also dismissed as being not maintainable.</u>

<u>3)	However, the order passed by the Tribunal under Section 193C (3) in confirming, modifying, annulling the decision of the Review Committee or sending the case back to the Review Committee on remand is an order under Section 196B and hence Appeal against such order passed by the Tribunal shall lie before the High Court Division under Section 1960 of the said Act. Thus, Customs Appeal No. 25 of 2008 is maintainable and the same is allowed. Customs Authority is directed to accept CRF value for the final assessment and release the bank guarantee of the appellant within 30(thirty) days from receipt of the copy of this judgment and order.</u>

28. Before we depart, we like to convey our deep gratitude to both the Amicus Curiae and the learned advocates who appeared before us Office if directed to send a copy of this judgment and order to the respondent No. 1 in all the appeals under the seal and signature of an officer of the High Court Division in view of sub-section (3) of Section 1960 of the said Act.

Send down the record of the lower authority.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Emdadul Huq J : Subject-matter of the Rule: The dispute raised in this case relates to the election of Trade Union named Gas Transmission Company Karmachari Union (shortly the Trade Union). Two groups of people, being the two petitioners on the one side and respondent No; 3 and some others on the other, claim to be the elected office bearers of the Trade Union. The opposing claims of the two groups resulted in BLA Case No. 642 of 2014 and the 2nd Labour Court, Dhaka passed order dated 24-9-2014.This order was set aside by the judgment dated 15-12-2015 passed by the Labour Appellate Tribunal (shortly the Appeal Tribunal) in Appeal No. 595 of 2014. This judgment is under challenge in this writ petition.

2. Earlier a Rule Nisi was issued in this case about the lawful authority of the Appeal Tribunal in passing the said judgment dated 15-12-2014 and also about the legality thereof.

3. By that judgment the Appeal Tribunal directed respondent No. 4 being the Director of Labour arid Registrar of Trade Unions (shortly the Labour Director) to supply to the appellant i.e. the present respondent No. 3 a copy of the list of office bearers of the Trade Union as elected on 15- 5-2014. The Appeal Tribunal further directed the learned Chairman, Second Labour Court, Dhaka to dispose of BLA Case No. 642 of 2014 instituted by respondent No.3 for a direction so that the Labour Director supplied the said list.

4. Petitioners' case:

The two petitioners, Md Liakot Ali and Md Abdul Kader, claim that they are the workers of the Gas Transmission Company Ltd. (shortly the Company), and that they were elected as President and Secretary of the Trade Union for the tenure of 2009-2011.

5. However respondent No. 3 and some other people formed a new Trade Union under the name Gas Transmission Company Ltd., Karmachari League (shortly the Karmachari League) and obtained registration. So the petitioners filed BLA Case No. 15 of 2011 in the First Labour Court, Dhaka for cancellation of the registration of the Karmachari League as a Trade Union of the Company. In that case, the present respondent No. 3 stated on oath that he had relinquished the membership of the old Trade Union and joined the new Trade Union being the Karmachari League.

6. Subsequently the petitioners came across an undated application signed by respondent No. 3 for restoration of his membership of the old Trade Union. So the petitioners as President and Secretary, rejected that application on recorded reasons.

7. Due to pendency of the BLA case No. 15 of 2011, the election of the Trade Union for the tenure 2011-2013 could not be held. So the petitioners continued to hold their respective office of the Trade Union.

8. However, under demand of the members of the Trade Union the petitioners called a General Council Meeting on 7-5-2014. An Election Sub-committee was formed and election was held on the same day. In this election the two petitioners were elected for the next tenure of 2014-2016 as President and Secretary along with others. On 21-5-2014, the Election Sub-committee sent to the Labour Director (respondent No.4) the list of the newly elected office bearers of the Trade Union including those of the petitioners.

9. But the petitioners came to know that respondent No.3 has forged the signatures of the petitioners and others and prepared some documents showing a General Council Meeting of the Trade Union on 15-5-2014 and that some people also sent to the Labour Director the list of the office bearers of the Trade Union as being elected on 15-5-2014. So on 8-6-2014 the petitioners submitted a complaint to the Labour Director.

10. In the meantime, responded No.3 filed BLA Case No. 642 of 2014 in the 2nd Labour Court, Dhaka without impleading the petitioners as parties. So the petitioners filed an application for being added as parties to the case. After hearing both sides, the said Labour Court, by order dated 24-9-2014, allowed petitioners application and directed the Labour Director to conduct the election of the CBA/Executive Committee as per the directives of the High Court Division as contained in judgment dated 8-7-2014 passed in WP, No. 7372 of 2011 and No. 4316 of 2014.

11. Against that order, the present respondent No.3 as the First party of the said BLA Case No. 642 of 2014, preferred Appeal No. 595 of 2014 before the Appeal Tribunal. After hearing both sides, the Appeal Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, set aside the said order passed by the 2nd Labour Court and illegally directed the Labour Director to supply to respondent No.3 a copy of the list of the office bearers elected on 15-5-2014 within seven days from the receipt of that order. Hence the present writ petition.

12. Case of respondent No.3:

respondent No.3, Md Lutfur Rahman, has filed an affidavit-in-opposition. He admits that the two petitioners were the elected President and Secretary of the Trade Union for the tenure of 2009-2011 and that the respondent had once resigned as a member of the Trade Union.

13. However respondent No. 3 claims that the petitioners intentionally filed BLA Case No. 15 of 2011 to delay the election for the next tenure. So, for preventing the illegal activities of the petitioners, respondent No. 3 and others formed a new Trade Union called the Karmachari League, but respondent No.3 ultimately resigned from the Karmachari League, because of the delay in disposal of the BLA Case No. 15 of 2011 instituted by the petitioners. Then he applied to the petitioners for restoration of his membership of the old Trade Union (Karmachari Union) and it was duly accepted and he rejoined the old Trade Union on 14-12-2012.

14. Respondent No.3 further claims that no General Council Meeting of the Trade Union was held on 7-5-2014 as claimed by the petitioners. Rather a real General Council Meeting was held on 15-5-2014 and the respondent No.3 himself was duly elected as the President of the Trade Union along with other office bearers.

15. Accordingly respondent No.3 submitted an application to the Labour Director for supplying a list of the newly elected office bearers of the Trade Union, but the later delayed in supplying the list. So respondent No.3 filed BLA Case No. 642 of 2014 in the Second labour Court, Dhaka which passed order dated 24-9-2014 directing the Labour Director to hold fresh election. So respondent No. 3 preferred Appeal No. 595 of 2014 wherein the Appeal Tribunal passed the impugned judgment and order dated 15-12-2015.

16. Respondent No: J further claims that the petitioners filed a complaint dated 8-4-2014 to the Labour Director raising objection to the election of respondent No. 3 and others. But the petitioners, on 26-6-2014, withdrew their complaint

17. Respondent No.3 has stated that, in compliance with the direction of the Appeal Tribunal as contained in the impugned judgment, the Labour Director has already supplied to respondent No.3 the list of the elected office bearers of the Trade Union and therefore the Rule has become infructous and it should be discharged.

18. Deliberation at the hearing. At the hearing of this case, Mr Choudhury Sanwar Ali, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the impugned judgment and order dated 15-12-2014 passed by the Appeal Tribunal is a totally nonspeaking order and it is self-contradictory as well, because the Appeal Tribunal has, on the one hand, directed the Labour Director to supply the list of the disputed office bearers and, on the other, remanded the BLA Case to the Labour Court for disposal of the same dispute on merit.

19. Mr Choudhury, the learned Advocate, next submits that the subject matter of the pending BLA case is the legality of the election of the respondent No.3 and others as the office bearer of the Trade Union and it can be decided only upon recording evidence by the Labour Court which was not one, but the Appeal Tribunal without the support of any evidence, passed the direction and thereby pre-empted the adjudication of the dispute by the Labour Court.

20. Mr Choudhury, the learned Advocate, next submits that the Labour Director has in his written statement/ Report (Annexure-1 series-part), clearly stated the fact of existence of two rival group of claimants to be the elected office bearers of the same Trade Union and also about his inability to supply any list to any of the two groups, and yet the Appeal Tribunal observed that the said Report proves nothing.

21. Mr Choudhury, the learned Advocate next submits that the learned Chairman of the 2nd Labour Court Dhaka recorded his decision correctly, and yet the decision was illegal, because the order is silent as to whether the Labour Court was duly constituted as required by section 214 of the Labour Act, 2006 to the effect that the Labour Court shall consist of three persons, being the Chairman and one representative from the শ্রমিকপক্ষ and another from মালিকপক্ষ and decision is also silent as to whether the learned Chairman endeavored to obtain the non-binding opinion of the said representative.

22. Mr Choudhury, the learned Advocate next submits that in view of such illegality in the constitution of the Labour Court the Appeal Tribunal should have simply set aside the order passed by the Labour Court and should have remanded the BLA Case for disposal thereof on merit, and that the Appeal Tribunal should not have passed any direction to supply the list nor should have recorded any finding on the merit of the case.

23. Mr Choudhury, the learned Advocate next submits that, by the Rule issuing order, operation of the impugned judgment passed by Appeal Tribunal was stayed and therefore the fact of supply of any list by the Labour Director during pendency of this Rule was illegal and does not affect the disposal of this Rule on merit.

24. In reply Mr Md Mahbubul Haque, the learned Advocate for the respondent No.3, submits that the order dated 24-9-2014 passed by the Labour Court was illegal as the said court was not legally constituted and therefore the impugned judgment passed by the Appeal Tribunal setting aside the Labour Court's order was lawful and proper.

25. Mr Haque, the learned Advocate, next submits that the Appeal Tribunal was convinced that an election was duly held on 15-5-2014 and accordingly the said Tribunal passed the impugned judgment and order containing the direction to the Labour Director to supply the list of the elected office bearers, and it has been duly complied with by the Labour Director, and there is no legal bar to the adjudication of the pending BLA Case by the Labour Court.

26. Findings and Decisions:

It is evident that the dispute between the parties arose due to the fact that both groups claim to have been elected in the General Council Meeting allegedly held on two dates being on 7-5-2014 as claimed by the petitioners and on 15-5-2014 as claimed by respondent No.3.

27. It is further evident that, in the pending BLA Case No. 642 of 2014, the 1st party being present respondent No.3 has prayed for direction so that the Labour Director supplies to the 1st party (respondent No.3) the list of the elected office bearers.

28. In the above context, the other dated 24- 9-2014 (Annexure H) was passed by the 2nd Labour Court in BLA Case No. 642 of 2014. It appears that this order contains decision on two aspects namely allowing the application of the present petitioners for being added as second party to that case and direction to the Labour Director was directed to hold election of the Trade Union in accordance with the guidelines as recorded by another Division Bench of this Court in the judgment dated 8-7-2014 passed in WP No. 7372 of 2011 and WP No. 4316 of 2014.

29. Against the said order passed by the Labour Court, the 1st party being respondent No. 3 preferred Appeal No. 595 of 2014 and the Appeal Tribunal passed the impugned judgment dated 15-12-2014 (Annexure-I).

30. On perusal of this judgment (Annexure-I), it is revealed that the learned Advocates for both sides made submission before the Appeal Tribunal to the effect that, the members of the Labour Court were not present and that there was no effort on the part of the learned Chairman of the Labour Court to consult the members. The Appeal Tribunal recorded the following finding.

"I find substance in their submission and thus the impugned order dated 24-7-2012 passed by the learned Chairman Labour Court, Dhaka is hereby set aside."

31. There is nothing on record to show that the 2nd Labour Court, Dhaka while passing the order dated 29-9-2014 was duly constituted as required by section 214 of the Labour Act, 2006 to the effect that the Labour Court shall consist of three members, being the Chairman and two representatives. Similarly there is nothing on record to show that the learned Chairman before passing that order took any effort to obtain the non-binding opinion of the two representative members.

32. In view of such position, we hold that the order dated 24-9-2014 (Annexure-H) passed by the Second Labour Court, Dhaka in BLA Case No. 642 of 2014 was passed without lawful authority and was legally and correctly set aside by the Appeal Tribunal on the ground of lack of jurisdiction of the Chairman alone to act as Labour Court.

33. However the principal dispute raised in this writ petition is with regard to the 2nd part of the impugned judgment passed by the Appeal Tribunal which is quoted below:

"Further it appears from the letter dated 26-6-2014 that complaint against present appellant was withdrawn which proved that the contention of the appellant is legal. On the other hand a report was submitted by the Director of Labour which proves nothing.

Hence respondent No.1 is directed to supply certified copy of the list of Office Bearers elected on 15-5-2014 within 7(seven) days from the receipt of the copy of this order.

Meanwhile, the learned Chairman of the Labour Court below is directed to dispose of the case on merit after taking evidence preferably within 2 (two) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.

This order shall be treated to be final order subject to the decision of the Labour Court below".

34. It is evident that the Appeal Tribunal not only sent the BLA case on remand for disposal of the same on merit but also passed an interim direction to the Labour Director to supply the "list of Office Bearers elected on 15-5-2014 .... "

35. The petitioners claim to have been elected not on 15-5-2014, but on 7-5-2014, which means that this aspect of the dispute needs to be decided on merit upon recording evidence.

36. It further appears that, in passing the above direction the Appeal Tribunal recorded its own finding on two other questions of fact, namely withdrawal of the complaint lodged by the present petitioners, and the merit of the report submitted by the Labour Director.

37. With regard to the report of the Labour Director, the Appellate Tribunal recorded a finding that it "proves nothing". We find from the copy of the said Report (Annexure-L) that the Labour Director has stated the detailed facts with regard to the claim of the two rival groups as the elected office bearers of the same Trade Union and also about his inability to supply the list of office bearers to any of the rival groups.

38. In that report the Labour Director has further referred to the direction of this Court as contained in the judgment dated 8-7-2014 passed in Writ Petition Nos. 7372 of 20 11 and No. 4316 of 2014 with regard to guidelines for holding election under supervision of the Labour Director.

39. The claim of the two rival groups as stated by the Labour Director are disputed questions of fact that can only be adjudicated upon recording evidence and therefore the finding of the Appeal Tribunal that the aforesaid written statement/report submitted by the Labour Court "proves nothing" is not based on any legal evidence.

40. With regard to withdrawal of the complaint lodged by the petitioners, they have stated in this case that they never withdrew it and that the alleged withdrawal letter was a product of forgery. It is not clear as to the basis of the Appeal Tribunal's finding on the issue of withdrawal.

41. All the above noted questions of fact can be decided only upon recording proper evidence. But there is nothing on record to show that in the BLA Case No. 642 of 2014 any evidence was at all recorded. The Appeal Tribunal itself was also aware of this position and remanded the BLA Case for disposal on merit after recording evidence. So there was no legal scope on the part of the Appeal Tribunal to take decision on the aforesaid disputed questions of fact.

<u>42. It is noted that under section 216(1) and section 218(7) of Labour Act, 2006, the Labour Court and the Appeal Tribunal respectively has the lawful authority to act as a Civil Court and a Civil Appellate Court respectively in the matter of recording evidence and taking decision on a dispute other than those of criminal nature. This means that the Appeal Tribunal should not have recorded the aforesaid findings on the disputed questions of fact before any legal evidence was recorded. The Appeal Tribunal exercised its appellate jurisdiction in passing the impugned judgment not in accordance with law particularly section 218(7) of the Labour Act, 2006.</u>

43. Accordingly, we hold that the impugned judgment is liable to be partly set aside so far it relates to the finding that the present petitioners had withdrawn their complaint and so far it relates to direction to the Labour Director for supplying the list of the office bearers of the Trade Union.

44. The other part of the impugned judgment dated 15-12-2014 passed by the Appeal Tribunal namely on setting aside of the Labour Court's order dated 24-9-2014 and on remanding the BLA case was lawfully and correctly passed on the preliminary ground that the 2nd Labour Court, Dhaka was not duly constituted while passing its order dated 20-9-2014.

45. It appears from the copy of the judgment dated 8-7-2014 in Writ Petition No. 7372 of 2011 and W.P No. 4316 of 2014 that specific guidelines were given by another Division of this court about the manner of holding election of all Trade Unions under supervision of the Labour Director as per the Labour Act, 2006. So we further hold that those guidelines are to be followed in the case of election of the instant Trade Union.

46. In view of the above the Rule is made absolute in part. The impugned judgment and order dated 15-12-2014 passed by the Labour Appeal Tribunal in Appeal No. 595 of 2014 is hereby declared to be of no legal effect so far it relates to the positive finding on the withdrawal of the complaint lodged by the petitioners to the Labour Director and so far it relates to the direction given to the Labour Director (respondent No. 4) to supply a copy of the list of the office bearers of the Gas Transmission Company Karmachari Union,

47. The Second Labour Court, Dhaka is directed to hear BLA Case No. 642 of 2014 and to dispose of the same including the application of the petitioners to be added as party in accordance with law after following the requirements of sections 214, 216 and other provisions of the Labour Act, 2006. If the said Labour Court decides that election of any of the claimant groups was not held in accordance with law and the direction contained in the judgment passed in WP Nos. 7372 of 2011 and No. 4316 of 2014 the said Labour Court shall ensure that the election is to be held in accordance with law and keeping in view of the said directives.

Send at once a copy of this judgment and order to the Appellate Tribunal and also to the Second Labour Court, Dhaka.

No order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
মি. বিচারপতি শেখ মোঃ জাকির হোসেনঃ অত্র প্রথম বিবিধ আপীলটি উদ্ভব হইয়াছে খুলনা জেলা জজ আদালতের দেওয়ানী ১১৪/২০০৬ নং জারী মামলায় প্রচারিত ২০/০৭/২০১০ তারিখের রায় ও আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে, যে রায় ও আদেশ মূলে ১নং দায়িক-আপীলকারী ও ২-৯নং দায়িক প্রতিপক্ষদের বিরুদ্ধে ডিক্রিকৃত টাকা ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষের সঙ্গে যোগাযোগের মাধ্যমে নিজ দায়িত্বে পুনঃ তফসিলীকরণ করিতে পারিবেন মর্মে আদেশ হইয়াছে।

২। অতঃপর উক্ত রায় ও আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে সংক্ষুব্ধ হইয়া তাহার আইগত বৈধতার প্রতিবাদে ১নং দায়িক-আপীলকারী হিসাবে অত্র প্রথম বিবিধ আপীলটি দায়ের করেন এবং পরবর্তীতে উল্লেখিত জারী মামলার কাযক্রম অত্র প্রথম বিবিধ আপীল নিষ্পত্তি না হওয়া পযন্ত স্থগিতের নিমিত্তে এক দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিলে দরখাস্ত মঞ্জুর পূর্বক দেওয়ানী ১১৪/২০০৬ নং জারী মামলার কাযক্রম স্থগিত রাখার আদেশ হইলে দেওয়ানী ৫৩০(এফ.এম.)/২০১০নং রুলের উদ্ভব হয়। যেহেতু একই বিষয় নিয়া অত্র প্রথম বিবিধ আপীলি এবং দেওয়ানী রুলটি একটি মাত্র রায়ের মাধ্যমে নিস্পত্তির জন্য একই সঙ্গে শুনানীর জন্য গ্রহণ করা হইল।

৩। আপীল ও রুলটি নিস্পত্তির স্বার্থে সংক্ষিপ্ত ঘটনা এই যে, ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ দরখাস্তকারী হিসাবে বকেয়া গৃহ ঋণ আদায়ের নিমিত্তে খুলনা জেলা জজ আদালতে ১নং দায়িক-আপীলকারীসহ ২-৯নং প্রতিপক্ষদের বিরুদ্ধে ৩১/০৭/১৯৯৬ তারিখ পযন্ত সুদ এবং আসলসহ ১৪,৫৬,৬১৭.৭২ টাকা আদায়ের নিমিত্তে বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন অর্ডার ১৯৭৩ এর ২৭ ধারার বিধান অনুযায়ী ২৯/০১/১৯৯৭ তারিখে বিবিধ ৩১/১৯৯নং মামলা দায়ের করেন। উক্ত মামলায় দায়িক-আপীলকারী ২-৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ ঋণ গ্রহীতাগণ লিখিত আপত্তি দাখিল করেন। কিন্তু কোন সাক্ষ্যাদি উপস্থাপন করেন নাই। অতঃপর বিজ্ঞ জেলা জজ ডিক্রিদার-১ নং প্রতিপক্ষ দরখাস্তকারীর দরখাস্ত এবং তাহাদের পক্ষে উপস্থাপিত ১জন সাক্ষীর সাক্ষ্যাদি এবং দাখিলীয় কাগজপত্রাদি পর্যালোচনা ও মূল্যায়ন করিয়া ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ-দরখাস্তকারীর প্রত্যাশিত মতে ১৪,৫৬,৬১৭.৭২ টাকা আদায় পযন্ত সুদ এবং খরচসহ ডিক্রি দেন, অন্যথায় বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি এবং তদুপরিস্থ বিল্ডিং-ইমারতাদি আদালতের মাধ্যমে বিক্রয় করিয়া ডিক্রির টাকা আদায় পযন্ত সুদসহ খরচা সমন্বয় করিতে পারিবেন।

৪। অতঃপর উক্ত রায় ও ডিক্রির পর দায়িক-আপীলকারী এবং ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষগন ডিক্রির টাকা পরিশোধ না করায় দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার ১নং প্রতিপক্ষ ২৬/০১/২০০৬ তারিখের আদালতের রায়ের আলোকে ডিক্রি জারীর নিমিত্তে যে দরখাস্ত দায়ের করেন, তাহা দেওয়ানী ১১৪/২০০৬নং জারী মামলা হিসাবে রুজু হয়।

৫। অতঃপর উক্ত জারী মামলায় ১নং দায়িক-আপীলকারী সহ ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষ হাজির হইয়া ডিক্রিকৃত ১৪,৫৬,৬১৭.৭২ টাকা মাসিক ৮,৬০০/- টকা হারে ১৬৯টি কিস্তিতে পরিশোধ পূর্বক কিস্তির প্রার্থনা করিলে বিজ্ঞ আদালত ০৮/১০/২০০৭ তারিখের ১১নং আদেশে ৩ লক্ষ টাকা জমা দানের নির্দেশ প্রদান করেন, যাহার পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে আপীলকারী এবং ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষদের পক্ষ হইতে মে, ২০১০ পযন্ত সর্বমোট ৪,৪৮,০০০/- টাকা পরিশোধ করা হয়। তদুপরি বিগত ২৩/০৫/২০১০ তারিখ দায়িক-আপীলকারী ও ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষদের পক্ষ হইতে তাহাদের পরিশোধিত ৪,৪৮,০০০/- টাকা দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ কর্পোরেশনের প্রকাশিত সার্কুলার নং যথাক্রমে ২/২০০৮ ও ২/২০০৯ এর মর্ম অনুযায়ী বকেয়া টাকার শতকরা ৩০% হিসাবে গণ্য করিয়া সমন্বয় পূর্বক অবশিষ্ট টাকা পুনঃতফসিলীকরণের প্রার্থনা করেন। যাহা ২০/০৭/২০১০ তারিখে ৩৯নং আদেশ মূলে নিম্নোক্ত মর্মে নিস্পত্তি করা হয়।
“দায়িপক্ষ হাজিরা দাখিল করিয়াছে। ডিক্রিদারপক্ষ হাজিরা দাখিল করে নাই। ঋণের টাকা কিস্তিতে পরিশোধের জন্য দায়িপক্ষের দাখিলী দরখাস্ত (১১/০৩/২০০৭ তারিখের) শুনানীর জন্য উপস্থাপন করা হইল।
শুনিলাম। দায়িকপক্ষের পুনঃতফসিলীকরণের বিষয়টি ডিক্রিদার নিজ দায়িত্বে করিলে করিতে পারিবেন। আগামী ২৪/০৮/২০১০ তারিখ ডিক্রিদার পক্ষের তদবিরের জন্য দিন ধায হইল।”

৬। উক্ত রায় ও আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে সংক্ষুব্ধ হইয়া ১নং দায়িক আপীলকারী হিসাবে অত্র প্রথম বিবিধ আপীলটি দায়ের করিয়াছেন।

৭। আপীলকারীপক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি আপীলের স্বপক্ষে নিবেদন করেন যে, দায়িক-আপীলকারীপক্ষ ডিক্রিকৃত টাকা ১৬৯টি কিস্তিতে পরিশোধসহ পুনঃতফসিলীকরণের জন্য নিম্ন আদালতে ১১/০৩/২০০৭ তারিখে দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিলে বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতের নির্দেশে বিভিন্ন তারিখে ৩লক্ষ টাকা এবং পরবর্তীতে আরো টাকা পরিশোধ করেন। সর্বোপরি মে, ২০১০ পযন্ত দায়িক-আপীলকারী ও ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষ ডিক্রিকৃত টাকার বিপরীতে ৪,৪৮,০০০/- টাকা পরিশোধ করিয়াছেন এবং আদালতের এই টাকার কিস্তি চলমানকালে দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষের দপ্তর হইতে বকেয়া ঋণ পরিশোধের জন্য ২টি সার্কুলার যথা ০২/০৮ ও ০২/০৯ জারী করা হয়। যেখানে শর্ত থাকে যে, বকেয়া পাওনার উপর শতকরা ১৫-৩০% ভাগ টাকা জমা প্রদান করিলে বকেয়া পাওনা পুনঃতফসিলীকরণ করা হইবে। কিন্তু যেহেতু বকেয়া পাওনা কিস্তিতে পরিশোধের নিমিত্তে দাখিলকৃত ১১/০৩/২০০৭ তারিখের দরখাস্ত নিম্ন আদালতে বিচারাধীণ ছিল এবং বিজ্ঞ আদালতের নির্দেশেই দায়িক-আপীলকারী ও ২-৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষের প্রকাশিত উল্লেখিত সার্কুলারের সুযোগ সুবিধা গ্রহন করিতে পারেন নাই। তদুপরি পরবর্তীতে আদালতের নির্দেশে জমাকৃত টাকা মূল বকেয়ার ৩০% হিসাবে গণ্য করিয়া ঋণটি পুনঃতফসিলীকরণের নিবেদন করেন। কিন্তু বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত তাহা অযৌক্তিকভাবে অগ্রাহ্যপূর্বক বিষয়টি দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষের উপর চাপিয়ে দিয়া যে আদেশ প্রদান করিয়াছেন তাহা ন্যায় বিচারের পরিপন্থী। বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি আরো নিবেদন করেন যে, কিস্তির বিষয়টি যখন দায়িক-আপীলকারীপক্ষ সর্বপ্রথম বিজ্ঞ আদালতের নজরে আনেন তখন যদি দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষের সঙ্গে যোগাযোগ করার নির্দেশ দিতেন তাহা হইলে দায়িক-আপীলকারীপক্ষ সেই সুযোগ গ্রহণ করার সুবিধা ভোগ করিতে পারিতেন। অথচ বিজ্ঞ আদালত দায়িক-আপীলকারী ও ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষদের কিস্তির বিপরীতে ৩লক্ষ টাকা জমা দেওয়ার নির্দেশ প্রদান করিয়া দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার ১নং প্রতিপক্ষ কর্তৃক ঘোষিত সার্কুলার অনুযায়ী প্রদত্ত সুযোগ সুবিধা হইতে বঞ্চিত করিয়াছেন। বর্তমানে আদলতের এই কৌশলগত আদেশের জন্য দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ তাহাদের মোট বকেয়া পাওনার হিসাবে ২৯,৬১,৫৫০.৬০ টাকা দাবী করিতেছেন যাহা সম্পূর্ণরূপে বেআইনী, সংবিধান পরিপন্থী, এমনকি আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের ঋণ আদায়ের প্রচলিত আইনের চরম ব্যত্যয় ঘটে। বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি আরো নিবেদন করেন যে, দায়িক-আপীলকারীপক্ষ হইতে যে টাকা ইতোপূর্বে বিজ্ঞ আদালতের নির্দেশ মতে জমা প্রদান করা হইয়াছে তাহা বর্তমান পাওনার সঙ্গে সমন্বয় করা হয় নাই। সর্বোপরি বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি নিবেদন করেন যে, দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষের মূল ঋণের ২০০% (১০০+২০০=৩০০) বেশী উল্লেখিত দাবী সম্পূর্ণরূপে অযৌক্তিক, অগ্রহনযোগ্য এবং আইনের পরিপন্থী বিধায়, তাহা রদ ও রহিতযোগ্য এবং দায়িক-আপীলকারীরপক্ষ ২৬/০১/২০০৬ তারিখের ডিক্রিকৃত টাকা কিস্তিতে প���িশোধসহ পুনঃতপসিলীকরণ পাইতে হকদার এবং সেই পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে অত্র আপীলটি মঞ্জুর হওয়ার নিবেদন করেন।

৮। ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষে বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি নিবেদন করেন যে, দায়িক-আপীলকারীর দাখিলকৃত অত্র প্রথম বিবিধ আপীলটি এবং তৎপরিপ্রেক্ষিতে উদ্ভূত দেওয়ানী রুলটি আইনতঃ রক্ষনীয় নহে। ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ প্রতিষ্ঠানটি ১৯৭৩ সালে মহামান্য রাষ্ট্রপতির (পরবর্তীতে পি.ও হিসাবে অবিহিত হইবে) ৭নং আদেশের বলে প্রতিষ্ঠিত এবং উক্ত আদেশের বিধি-বিধান অনুযায়ী বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন তথা ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ কর্পোরেশন পরিচালনাসহ তাহাদের কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ঋণ কি পদ্ধতিতে আদায় হইবে তাহার বর্ণনা রহিয়াছে এবং অত্র আদেশটি একটি বিশেষ আইন হিসাবে স্বীকৃত এবং এই বিশেষ আইনের বিশেষত্ব অনুযায়ী এই আইনের বা আদেশের বিধান অনুযায়ী দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ বকেয়া ঋণ আদায়ের নিমিত্তে দায়িক-আপীলকারী ও ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষদের বিরুদ্ধে খুলনার জেলা জজ আদালতে বিবিধ ৩১/১৯৯৭নং মামলা দায়ের করেন। যেখানে দায়িক-আপীলকারী এবং ২-৯ নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষগণ হাজির হইয়া লিখিত আপত্তি দাখিল করেন। দায়িক-আপীলকারী এবং ২-৯নং প্রতিপক্ষগণ ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ কর্পোরেশনের নিকট হইতে ০৭/০৩/১৯৮৮ তারিখে শতকরা ১০% ভাগ সুদের হারে ৭,৭২,০০০/- টাকা গৃহ নির্মান ঋaণ গ্রহন করেন, যাহার বিপরীতে নালিশী দরখাস্তের তফসিলে বর্ণিত ভূমি তদুপরিস্থ নির্মানাদি রেজিস্ট্রিকৃত দলিলমূলে বন্ধক/রেহেন রাখেন। কিন্তু দায়িক-আপীলকারীসহ ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষগণ ৩১/০৭/৯৬ তারিখ পযন্ত কিস্তির কোন টাকা পরিশোধ না করায় সুদ এবং আসল বাবদ ১৪,৫৬,৬১৭.৭২ টাকা এবং আদায় না হওয়া পযন্ত তাহার উপর সুদ আরোপের প্রার্থনার নিমিত্তে উক্ত মামলা দায়ের করেন।

৯। অতঃপর মামলাটি দো-তরফা সূত্রে ২৬/০১/২০০৬ তারিখে দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষের প্রার্থীত মতে রায় ও ডিক্রি হয়। দায়িকপক্ষগণ রায় ও ডিক্রির শর্ত নির্দিষ্ট সময়ের মধ্যে প্রতিপালন না করায় ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ কর্পোরেশন ডিক্রি জারীর নিমিত্তে দেওয়ানী ১১৪/০৬নং জারী মামলা দায়ের করেন। অতঃপর উক্ত জারীর মামলায় দায়িক-আপীলকারীপক্ষ বিজ্ঞ আদালতের নিকট কিস্তিসহ পুনঃতফসিলীকরণের প্রার্থনা করিলে তাহা দায়িকপক্ষ নিজ দায়িত্বে করিতে পারিবেন মর্মে আদেশ প্রদান করিলে, উক্ত রায় ও আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে সংক্ষুব্ধ হইয়া দায়িকপক্ষ অত্র আপীলটি দায়ের করিয়াছেন। বর্তমানে দায়িক-আপীলকারী ও ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষদের নিকট দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষের বকেয়া পাওনার পরিমান দাড়িয়েছে ২৯,৬১,৫৫০.৬০ টাকা। যেহেতু বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন আদেশ ১৯৭৩ একটি বিশেষ বিধান এবং এই বিশেষ বিধানের আওতায়ই দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ দরখাস্তকারী হিসাবে প্রতিকারের প্রার্থনার নিমিত্তে দরখাস্ত দায়ের করিয়াছেন এবং তাহারই পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে দায়িক-আপীলকারী ও ২-৯নং দায়িক-প্রতিপক্ষদের বিরুদ্ধে যথার্থ রায় ও আদেশ প্রদান করিয়াছেন এবং ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ হালনাগাদ পযন্ত সুদসহ মূল টাকা আদায়ের হকদার বটে। এই ক্ষেত্রে, দায়িক-আপীলকারীপক্ষে বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবির বক্তব্য তথা অর্থঋণ আদালতের বিধান অত্র মামলার ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য নহে। কেননা, বাংলাদেশ হাউস বির্ল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন তাহাদের নিজস্ব বিধান অনুযায়ী ঋণ আদায়ের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করিতে পারিবেন অথবা অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের বিধানেও প্রতিকার প্রার্থনার সুযোগ আছে, যাহা মীমাংসিত সিদ্ধান্ত। বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি আরো নিবেদন করেন যে, যেহেতু ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন অর্ডার ১৯৭৩ এর বিশেষ বিধান অনুযায়ী অত্র মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করিয়াছেন, সেহেতু উক্ত আইন বা আদেশের বিধান অনুযায়ী অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি নিস্পত্তি হইবে। এক্ষেত্রে অন্য কোন আইনের কর্তৃত্ব প্রযোজ্য হইবে না। সর্বশেষ, বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি নিবেদন করেন যে, দায়িক-আপীলকারী আইনের কোন অসংগতির বিষয়ে কোন প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন করিলে আইনের অসংগতিকে চ্যালেঞ্জ করিয়া এবং সেই সংক্রান্তে রুল জারী হইলে কেবল তখনই উক্ত বিষয়ে প্রতিকার পাওয়ার সুযোগ পাইতে পারেন। বর্তমান এখতিয়ারে দায়িক-আপীলকারীপক্ষের কোন প্রতিকার পাওয়ার কোন সুযোগ নাই বিধায়, আপীলটি নামঞ্জুরসহ রুলটি খারিজের প্রার্থনা করেন।

১০। উভয়পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবিদের উপরোক্ত মূল বক্তব্যের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে আমাদের সামনে মূখ্য এবং প্রধান বিচার্য্য বিষয় দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার কর্পোরেশন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কিনা এবং বকেয়া ঋণ আদায়ের ক্ষেত্রে দায়েরকৃত মামলা কোন এখতিয়ারে বা কোন আইনের বিধানবলে প্রযোজ্য হইবে? এবং আপীলকারী অত্র আপীলে আর কোন প্রতিকার পাইতে পারেন কিনা?

১১। বিষয়টি নিস্পত্তির ক্ষেত্রে প্রথমত আমাদেরকে দরখাস্তকারী কর্পোরেশনের চারিত্রিক বা কাঠামোগত অবস্থান তথা বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কিনা সেই বিষয়ে আলোকপাত করিতে হইবে। এই বিষয়ে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণের ক্ষেত্রে অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের পূর্বাপর অবয়ব পর্যালোচনার দাবী রাখে।

১২। অর্থঋণ আদালত অধ্যাদেশ ১৯৮৯ সালের ১৩/১১/১৯৮৯ তারিখে বাংলাদেশের মহামান্য রাষ্ট্রপতির ঘোষিত ১৬নং অধ্যাদেশ বলে জারী হয়। যেখানে মুখবন্ধে উল্লেখ থাকে যে,-
“আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক ঋণ আদায়ের জন্য বিশেষ বিধান প্রনয়নকল্পে প্রণীত।
অধ্যাদেশ-
সেহেতু আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ঋণ আদায়ের জন্য বিশেষ বিধান করা সমীচীন ও প্রয়োজনীয় এবং যেহেতু সংসদ অধিবেশনে নাই এবং রাষ্ট্রপতির নিকট ইহা সন্তোষজনকভাবে প্রতীয়মান হইয়াছে যে, আশু ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের জন্য প্রয়োজনীয় পরিস্থিতি বিদ্যমান রহিয়াছে; সেহেতু গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশের সংবিধানের ৯৩(১) অনুচ্ছেদে প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে রাষ্ট্রপতি নিম্নরূপ অধ্যাদেশ প্রণয়ন ও জারী করিলেন।”
উক্ত অধ্যাদেশের ২নং ধারায় আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান এবং আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানগুলির নাম উল্লেখ থাকে। যেখানে বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশনের নাম ২(ক)(৩)নং উপ-ধারায় উল্লেখ থাকে।
উক্ত অধ্যাদেশের ৩ ধারার বক্তব্য নিম্নরূপঃ
“৩। অন্যান্য আইনের প্রয়োগ। এই অধ্যাদেশের বিধানাবলী, উহাতে ভিন্নরূপ কিছু না থাকিলে, আপাততঃ বলবৎ অন্য কোন আইনের অতিরিক্ত; এবং উহার হানিকর নয় বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে।”
এবং ৯ ধারার বক্তব্য নিম্নরূপঃ
“৯। বিচারাধীন মামলা। আপাততঃ বলবৎ অন্য কোন আইনে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, ঐ অধ্যাদেশ প্রবর্তনের অব্যবহিত পূর্বে কোন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের ঋণ আদায় সংক্রান্ত কোন মামলা কোন আদালতে বিচারাধীন থাকিলে উহা উক্ত আদালতেই নিস্পত্তি করা হইবে এবং এই অধ্যাদেশ উক্ত মামলার ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য হইবে না।”
সেখানেও আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের সংজ্ঞা এবং আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের নামের ক্রমিকে বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশনের নাম উল্লেখ আছে।

১৩। অর্থঋণ আদালত অধ্যাদেশ আইনের উপরোক্ত বর্ণনা  মতে বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশনের অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের ২ ধারা অনুযায়ী যেমন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান তেমনি আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের ক্রমিকে বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশনের নাম উক্ত আইনে সুস্পষ্টভাবে প্রতিয়মান যে, অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের বিধান অনুযায়ী বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন একটি আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান।

১৪। ডিক্রিদার-প্রতিপক্ষে কর্পোরেশনের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি নিবেদন করেন যে, যেহেতু ডিক্রিদার কর্পোরেশনের ঋণ আদায়ের ক্ষেত্রে নিজস্ব বি���ি-বিধান বা আইন আছে, সেহেতু অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন এর বিধি-বিধান দরখাস্তকারী কর্পোরেশনের পক্ষে প্রয়োগযোগ্য নহে। বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন অর্ডার ১৯৭৩ এর মুখবন্ধ তথা কি উদ্দেশ্যে উক্ত অর্ডার জারী করা হইল তাহা অনুধাবনের জন্য অর্ডারের মূখবন্ধ নিম্নে অনুলিখন করা হইল;

“Where it is expedient to provide for the establishment of the Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation for the purposes of providing financial facilities for the construction, repair and remodeling of house [at any place]1 in Bangladesh.”

	উক্ত মূখবন্ধে উল্লেখিত বাক্যটি হইতে সুস্পষ্ট যে, আদেশটি জারীর মূখ্য উদ্দেশ্য বাংলাদেশের নাগরিকদের বাড়ী নির্মাণ, মেরামত, সংস্কারের জন্য আর্থিক সহযোগীতা করা এবং ২৬ ও ২৭ অনুচ্ছেদে ঋণ আদায়ের সংক্ষিপ্ত বিধান রহিয়াছে। বিষয়টি স্পস্টীকরণের জন্য ২৬ এবং ২৭ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুলিখন করা হইল;

"26. (1) When a borrower or his surety makes default in repayment [ it or otherwise fails to comply with the terms of the agreement or letter of guarantee with the Corporation, the Corporation notwithstanding the provisions of any other law may, without the intervention of any Court, sell any property pledged, mortgaged, hypothecated or assigned by the borrower or his surety, to the Corporation by way of security. 
(2) Any tansfer of property made by the Corporation in exercise of its powers under clause (1) shall vest in the transferee all rights in or to the property transferred as if the property had been sold to the transferee by the owner. 
(3) All sums due to the Corporation from the borrower or his surety shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue. 

27. (1) Where by reason of the breach of any agreement by the borrower the Corporation becomes entitled to require the immediate payment of the amount due by the borrower to the Corporation, any officer of the corporation authorised generally or specially by the Board in this behalf may apply to the District Judge within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the borrowers house is situated for any one or more of the following relief, namely ; 
(a) an order for the sale of any property or properties pledged, mortgaged, hypothecated or assigned to the Corporation as security for the sums due by the borrower; 
(b) for an injuction restraining the borrower or his surety from in any manner removing, transferring or disposing of any of the properties .referred to in Sub-clause (a) ; 
(c) for an ad-interim attachment attaching the properties referred to in sub-clause (a) above and such other properties of the borrower or his surety as in the opinion of the District Judge were sufficient to cover the claim of the Corporation against the borrower including costs and interest. 
(2) An application under clause (1) shall state the nature and extent of the liability of the borrower and his surety to the Corporation, the grounds on which it is made and such other particulars as may be prescribed. 
(3) The District Judge may if he thinks fit hear the applicant and where the reliefs mentioned in sub-clauses (b) and (c) of clause (1) are prayed for in the application shall pass adinterim orders granting such reliefs as in the opinion of the District Judge are sufficient to safegaurd the full claim of the corporation against the borrower. 
(4) At the time of passing his orders under clause (3) the District Judge shall order notice of the application to issue to the borrower and his surety together with copies of the applications, the order passed by the District Judge under clause (3), and any evidence which may have been recorded at the time of the order under clause (3), calling upon the borrower and his surety to show cause on a date to be specified in the notice, why the interim orders passed should not be confirmed and the reliefs sought in the application be granted. 
(5) If no cause is shown on or before the date specified in the notice under clause (4), the District Judge shall dispose of the application. 
(6) If the borrower and his surety appear and show cause, the District Judge shall grant them and the Corporation reasonable opportunity to produce their evidence relating to the reliefs claimed in the application, and after, considering such evidence and hearing the parties, the District Judge shall pass his order disposing of the application. 
(7) When passing his order under clause (5) or clause (6) the District Judge shall—
(a) record his finding as to the amount due by the borrower to the corporation, and the interest payable thereon; 
(b) direct or refuse to direct the sale of the properties attached; 
(c) confirm, discharge or vary any ad-interim orders passed restraining the borrower and his surety or attaching their properties; and 
(d) pass any other incidental orders. 
(8) No order passed by the District Judge ordering the release of any property of the borrower or his surety from attachment shall be given effect to until after the expiry of 30 (thirty) days from the date of that order except with the written consent of the Corporation, or where an appeal has been preferred to the High Court Division, under the orders of the High Court Division. 
(9) An order under this Article for the attachment or sale of property shall be carried into effect as far as may be in the manner provided in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for the attachment or sale of property in execution of a decree as if the Corporation were the decree-holder. 
(10) Any party aggrived by an order under clause (5) or clause (6) may within thirty days from the date of the order appeal to the High Court Division, and upon such appeal the High Court Division may after hearing the parties pass such orders as it thinks proper."

আদেশের ২৬ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুযায়ী আদালতের হস্তক্ষেপ ছাড়া বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি বিক্রির মাধ্যমে ঋণ আদায় এবং উক্ত ঋণকে বকেয়া রাজস্ব হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে মর্মে উল্লেখ আছে। অন্যদিকে, আাবার ২৭ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুযায়ী আদালতের আশ্রয় নেওয়ার বিধান আছে, যদিও তাহা নির্দিষ্ট আদালতে।

	১৫। আইন প্রণয়নের উদ্দেশ্য আইনের মূখবন্ধে নিহিত থাকে। যদিও মুখবন্ধ আইনের অংশ কিনা এ বিষয়ে বিভিন্ন সময়ে বিতর্ক হইয়াছে। অনেকের মতে ইহা আইনের অংশ নয় বরং উহার বাহিরের অংশ। Lord Holt এর মতে, মুখবন্ধ আইনের অংশ নয় কিন্তু উহা আইন প্রণয়নের উদ্দেশ্য ব্যাখ্যা করে (Mills vs. Wilkins (1703) KB 662) Lord Halsbury এর মতে, সংক্ষিপ্ত শিরোনামের ন্যায় মুখবন্ধও আইনের অবিচ্ছেদ্য অংশ (Halsbury, Law of England (3rd Edition) Vol-36, P-370, Para-544) Shobha Vs. State of U.P. AIR 1963 All 29, মামলায় এলাহাবাদ হাইকোর্টও একইরূপ মন্তব্য করেন।

মুখবন্ধ আইন প্রনয়নের উদ্দেশ্য বর্ণনা করে কিন বা ইহার প্রয়োজনীয়তা কি সে বিষয়ে আসাম হাইকোর্টের পযবেক্ষণ লক্ষ্যনীয়। AIR 1959 Asam 147, 151, Nil Kumar Vs. Deputy Commissioner মোকদ্দমায় সিদ্ধান্ত হয় যে,
"The preamble alone cannot be held to be conclusive of the intent and purpose of the legislation. The object, purpose and intent of the legislation have to be gathered from the various provisions of the statute itself and not merely from an isolated examination of the Preamble, which may indicate the primary object in view, but may not refer in detail to certain other objects, which are incidental and essential to the working out of the primary object of the legislation." 

	১৬। আইনের ‘Operative part’ এ কোন সংশয় দেখা দিলে সে ক্ষেত্রে মুখবন্ধের সাহায্য নিয়া আইন ব্যাখ্যা করিতে হয়। মুখবন্ধ আইনের উপক্রমণিকা হিসাবে কাজ করে। আইনের শিরোনাম এবং মুখবন্ধ আইন ব্যাখ্যার ক্ষেত্রে সহায়ক ভূমিকে পালন করা ছাড়াও ইহা আইন সভার উদ্দেশ্যের প্রতিফলন ঘটায়। AIR 1953 SC 404 Kedarnath Bajoria v. State of West Bengle মোকদ্দমায় ভারতীয় সুপ্রীম কোর্ট অনুরূপ মন্তব্য করেন। মুখবন্ধের গুরুত্ব অনুধাবন করে AIR 1960 SC 1080, 1097 Kochuni v. State of Madras মামলায় ভারতীয় সুপ্রীম কোর্ট মন্তব্য করেনঃ
"The Preamble of a statute is a key to the understanding of it and it is well established that it may legitimately be consulted to solve any ambiguity, or to fix the meaning of words which may have more then one, or to keep the effect of the Act within its real scope, whenever the enacting part is in any of these respects open to doubt."

মুখবন্ধ আইনের Enacting part কে অনুসরণ করে। AIR 1955 Bom, 363, Commissioner of Labour Vs. Associated Cement Companies Ltd. মামলায় সিদ্ধান্ত হয় যে,

"The Preamble may no doubt show the object of enacting a law, but you shall not infer from it the Legislature did not mean to go further than the declared object."
মুখবন্ধ আইনের Enacting part এর বিরোধ হলে Enacting part প্রাধান্য পায়।

আইন ব্যাখ্যার একটি প্রতিষ্ঠিত নীতি আইনে ব্যবহৃত ভাষা যেখানে পরিস্কার সেখানে মুখবন্ধের বক্তব্য পরিহার করতে হয়। কন্তিু যেখানে উহা অপরিষ্কার ও দ্ব্যর্থবোধক সেখানে মুখবন্ধ গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অনুষঙ্গ হিসাবে কাজ করে। 5 DLR 527, Pashruddin Vs- Jolekha Khatun মামলায় সিদ্ধান্ত হয় যে;
“কোন ঘটনা বা কোন অবস্থার পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে একটি আইন প্রণীত হইয়াছে উহার সংক্ষিপ্ত বিবরণ মুখবন্ধে বর্ণিত থাকে। ফলে ঐ আইনের বিভিন্ন অংশে বিবৃত বিধানাবলী সুষ্ঠুভাবে ব্যাখ্যা করার ক্ষেত্রে মুখবন্ধ গাইড হিসাবে কাজ করিয়া থাকে।”

আইনসভার উদ্দেশ্য অনুধাবণ করার ক্ষেত্রে মুখবন্ধ আইনের ব্যাখ্যায় গুরুত্বপূর্ণ ভূমিকা রাখিতে সক্ষম বলিয়া 51 DLR, 473, 477 Parveen and another Vs. State মামলায় মন্তব্য করা হয়; যেখানে সিদ্ধান্ত হয় যে;-
"The intention of the legislature is to be gathered from the preamble and other provisions of the law and if these provisions are clear and unambiguous, there is no scope for putting any construction on the provisions of the Act."

১৭। একথা স্বীকায যে, বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশনের বকেয়া পাওনা আদায়ের ক্ষেত্রে বর্ণিত পি.ও এর ২৬ ও ২৭নং অনুচ্ছেদ অনুযায়ী ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের বিধান আছে কিন্তু মুখবন্ধের সঙ্গে যেমন ২৬ ও ২৭নং অনুচ্ছেদ পরস্পর বিরোধী। তবে বিচার্য্য বিষয় যে উক্ত বিধানের/আদেশের একটি অনুচ্ছেদ আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের বকেয়া ঋণ আদায়ের ক্ষেত্রে পরিপূর্ণ আইন (আ্যাকট) নাকি ইনঅ্যাকটিমেন্ট তাহা বিবেচনার বিষয়। বিষয় দুইটি পাশাপাশি রাখিয়া পর্যালোচনা সহ মূল্যায়ণ করিলে দেখা যায় যে, অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ঋণ আদায়ের ক্ষেত্রে একটি বিশেষ পরিপূর্ণ এবং প্রায় পদ্ধতিগত আইন। অন্যদিকে, ডিক্রিদার কর্পোরেশনের আদেশের বিধানের তথা পি.ও ৭, ১৯৭৩ এর ২৭ অনুচ্ছেদ পরিপূর্ণ আইন নহে বরং তাহা আইনের পরিভাষায় Enactment বলিয়া গণ্য করা যায়। বিষয়টি স্পস্টীকরনের জন্য ‘Act’ এবং Enactment সম্পর্কে আলোচনায় দেখা যায় যে,- 
“আইনসভা কর্তৃক প্রণীত আইন ব্যতীত অন্যান্য বিধি বিধান ‘Enactment’ নামে অভিহিত। ‘Act’ বা আইন যে অর্থে ব্যবহৃত হয় ‘Enactment’ ঐ অর্থে ব্যবহৃত হয় না। ‘Act’ বলতে পুরো আইনটিকে বুঝায়, অপরপক্ষে ঐ ‘Act’ এর ধারা, উপ-ধারা বা অনুচ্ছেদকে ‘Enactment’ বলা হয়। AIR 1941, All ERP-499 Director, Public Prosecutions Vs. Lamb মামলায় সিদ্ধান্ত হয় যে, “An enactment may mean something other than an Act of Parliament, but an Act means an Act of Parliament, but an Act means an Act of Parliament.” 2KB-(1906) 140, Wakefield etc. Co. v. Vakefield Corporation মোকদ্দমায় সিদ্ধা���্ত হয় যে, ‘Act’ means the whole Act, whereas section or part of a section in any Act may be an enactment.” আবার ‘Enactment’ শব্দটি দ্বারা কি বুঝায় তাহা বুঝাতে গিয়া মুহম্মদ হাবিবুর রহমান ও আনিসুজ্জামান তাঁদের রচিত ‘আইন-শব্দকোষ’ গ্রন্থে বলা হইয়াছে, ‘Enactment’ বা ‘বিধিবদ্ধকরণ’ বলিতে পার্লামেন্ট আইন, সাধারণ যাজকসভার ব্যবস্থা, আদেশ অথবা একটি অপ্রধান আইন, কিংবা এগুলির অন্তর্ভূক্ত কোন বিশেষ বিধান (যেমন, বিশেষ কোন ধারা)বুঝায়।

১৮। যদি তর্কের খাতিরে উক্ত অনুচ্ছেদটিকে আইনের মর্যাদা দেওয়া হইলেও যখন দুইটি বিশেষ আইন সমজাতীয় হয় সেক্ষেত্রে ‘in pari meteria’ নীতি অনুসরণ করিতে হয়
‘in pari meteria’ এই শব্দের আক্ষরিক অর্থ ‘সমজাতীয় মামলায় বা অবস্থা। সংবিধি ব্যাখ্যার ক্ষেত্রে বর্ণিত শব্দগুচ্ছ একটি নীতি হিসাবে স্বীকৃত। এই নীতি অনুসারে যে সকল সংবিধি একই ব্যক্তি বা বস্তু সম্পর্কিত বা একই সাধারণ উদ্দেশ্য সম্বলিত হয়, সেক্ষেত্রে আইনসভার উদ্দেশ্য অনুধাবন করার জন্য ঐ সংবিধিগুলোকে একত্রে বিবেচনা করিতে হয়। আর এই নীতিটি প্রয়োগ করা হয় তখনই যখন একটি বিশেষ সংবিধি দ্ব্যর্থবোধক হয়। ল্যাটিন ‘in pari meteria’ শব্দের ইংরেজী প্রতিশব্দ ‘in the same matter’. একই বিষয়ে একাধিক আইন প্রচলিত থাকিলে ঐরূপ সব আইনের অর্থ একত্রে উদ্ধার করিতে হ। যাহাতে আইনগুলোর মধ্যে বিদ্যমান অসঙ্গতি চিহ্নিত করা সম্ভব হয়। আইন ব্যাখ্যার ক্ষেত্রে এই প্রবচনটি অতি প্রয়োজনীয়। এ প্রসঙ্গে Black’s Law Dictionary-তে উল্লেখ করা হইয়াছে;-

;-"It is a canon of construction that statutes that are in pari materia may be construed together, so that inconsistencies in one statute may be resolved by looking at another statute on the same subject."

কখন একটি আইন ‘in pari meteria’ হইবে এবং কখন হইবে না তাহা ব্যাখ্যা করা হয় 32 DLR (AD) 138, Director of Taxation and Excise V. Mehdi Ali Khan Panni মোকদ্দমার, যেখানে সিদ্ধান্ত হয় যে,

"... unless the statute is in pari materia, no language of a statute is to be interpreted with the help of the language of another statute or to take recourse to analogy but if the two statutes are in pad materia, the language of one can be,c, taken assistance of in interpreting the language of the other." 

অন্যদিকে 42 DLR (AD) Muhammad Julfikar v. Abul Kalam Chowdhury and others মোকদ্দমায় সিদ্ধান্ত হয় যে,  
"... Where the provisions of the later Act could only operate indirectly as an aid to the construction of words in the earlier Act those provisions can only be used for that purpose if certain conditions apply to the earlier Act when it is considered by itself."

১৯। অর্থঋণ আদালতের আইন প্রণয়নের উদ্দেশ্য হইতেছে আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানসমূহ হইতে বিশেষ করে অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের ২ ধারা অনুযায়ী সজ্ঞায়িত আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান এবং তথায় উল্লেখিত আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানসমূহ হইতে বকেয়া ঋণ আদায়ের পরিপূর্ণ এবং পদ্ধতিগত বিধানের সমন্বয়ে একটি বিশেষ আইন যদিও ডিক্রি জারীর ক্ষেত্রে দেওয়ানী কাযবিধির বিধানকে অনুসরণের নিয়ম প্রয়োগযো্গ্য। কিন্তু ডিক্রিদার কর্পোরেশনের বকেয়া ঋণ আদায়ের বিধানটি অসম্পূর্ণ, অপূর্ণাঙ্গ এবং বিধিবদ্ধ পদ্ধতির অভাব সম্বলিত। অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনে ঋণ গ্রাহক দায়িকদের যে সকল সুযোগ-সুবিধা প্রদান করা হইয়াছে তাহা প্রধানতঃ
