১ ৷ ধারা ৭ মতে বহুল প্রচারিত জাতীয় দৈনিক ও স্থানীয় পত্রিকায় (যদি থাকে) সমন জারী সম্পর্কিত বিজ্ঞাপন আকারে প্রকাশের বিধান করার বিবাদী মোকদ্দমা সম্পর্কে অবগত হয়, বিবাদীর অজ্ঞাতে এক তরফা ডিক্রি হওয়ার সম্ভাবনা নাই ৷ মোকদ্দমার সমন জারী হওয়া/না হওয়ার বিষয়ে কোন দ্বিধা দ্বন্দ্ব থাকে না ৷
২ ৷ ধারা ১২(৮) এর শর্ত মতে আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক ঋণ গ্রহীতার সম্পত্তি ঋণ ও বন্ধক হিসাবে রাখা হয় তাহা নিলামে বিক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রে কোনরূপ অবৈধতা বা পদ্ধতিগত অনিয়ম থাকিলে সম্পত্তি জামানত প্রদানকারী ঋণ গ্রহীতা আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের বিরুদ্ধে ক্ষতিপূরণ দাবী করার বিধান বরা হয়।

৩ ৷ ধারা ১৪ মতে মামলা শুনানী মূলতবী সম্পর্কিত বিধান মোকদ্দমার শুধু বিবাদীর প্ৰতি প্রযোজ্য নহে।উক্ত বিধান মোকদ্দমার বাদী তথা আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের উপর প্রযোজ্য বাদীর প্রার্থনায় মূলতবীর ক্ষেত্রে আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানকেও মূলতবী খরচ প্রদান করতে হয় ৷

8 ৷ ধারা ২১ মতে মীমাংস সভা/ধারা ২২ মধ্যস্থতার মাধ্যমে মোকদ্দমা নিস্পত্তির সুযোগ থাকায় আলাপ আলোচনার মাধ্যমে সহজভাবে পারস্পরিক সমস্যা উপলব্ধি করিয়া সহজ সমাধানে আসা যায় ৷ উক্ত অবস্থায় পক্ষবৃন্দ দাখিলী কোর্ট ফি ফেরৎ পায় ৷

৫ ৷ ধারা ২৮ মতে জারী মামলা দাখিলের সময়সীমা আরোপ করার দায়িক ডিক্রিদারের বিলম্বিত দাবীর হাত হইতে রক্ষা পায় ৷

৬। ধারা ৩০ মতে বহুল প্রচারিত জাতীয় দৈনিক ও স্থানীয় পত্রিকায় নোটিশ জারী সম্পর্কিত বিজ্ঞাপন আকারে প্রকাশের বিধান করার দায়িক মোকদ্দমা সম্পর্কে অবগত হয়, দায়িকের অজ্ঞাতে একতরফা নিস্পত্তি হওয়ার সম্ভাবনা নাই। মোকদ্দমার নোটিশ জারী হওয়া/না হওয়ার বিষয়ে কোন দ্বিধা থাকে না ৷

৭ । ধারা ৪৪(৩) মতে আপীল দায়েরের সময় অন্তবর্তীকালীণ আদেশের বিষয়ে ক্ষুব্ধ হইলে তৎবিষয়েও প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা বরা যায় ৷

৮ ৷ ধারা ৪৬ মতে মামলা দায়ের সম্পর্কিত বিশেষ বিধান ও সময়সীমা আরোপ করার আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক বিলম্বিত দায়েরী মোকদ্দমায় বিশাল দাবীর অমানবিক থাবা হইতে ঋণ গ্রহীতা রক্ষা পায় ৷

৯। ধারা 8 ৭ মতে দাবী আরোপে সীমাবদ্ধতা করার ঋণ গ্রহীতা আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের প্রদত্ত আসল ঋণ অপেক্ষা ২০০% অর্থাৎ ১০০+২০০=৩০০ টাকার অধিক টাকা পরিশোধ করিতে হয় না ৷ অতীতে দেখা গিয়াছে যে ১ লক্ষ টাকা ঋণ দেওয়ার ১৫/১৬ বৎসর পর মামলা দায়েরে সুদাসলে ১৪/১৫ টাকা দাবী করিয়া ডিক্রি লাভ করে ৷ বর্ণিত বিধানের কারণে বর্তমানে তাহা সম্ভব নহে । অর্থাৎ বর্তমানে আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান ঋণ গ্রহীতার বিরুদ্ধে ১ লক্ষ টাকার ঋণের বিপরীতে ৩ লক্ষ টাকার অধিক দাবী করিতে পারিবে না ৷

১০ ৷ ধারা ৪৯ মতে ঋণের কিস্তির বিধানও করা যায় । ফলে দায়িকের আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে বা আদালত স্বীয় উদ্যোগে যথাযথ মনে করিলে দায়িককে ডিক্রিকৃত টাকা ১ (এক) বছরে ৪ (চার) টি সমান কিস্তিতে পরিশোধের জন্য সুযোগ দিতে পারে ৷ এমনকি ডিক্রিদার সম্মত থাকিলে ডিক্রিকৃত টাকা ৩ (তিন) বছরে ১২ (বার) টি সমান কিস্তিতে পরিশোধের জন্য আদালত দায়িককে সুযোগ দেওয়ার বিধান করা হয় ৷

১১ । ধারা ৫০ মতে আদালত আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের আরোপিত বেআইনী ও অন্যায় সুদ বা মুনাফা বা ভাড়া হ্রাস মাফ করিতে পারে ৷ ফলে আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান ঋণের উপর বে-আইনী সুদ/মুনাফা/ভাড়া আরোপ করিলে আদালত তাহা মাফ করিতে পারে বলিয়া আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান ঋণের উপর বে-আইনী সুদ/মুনাফা/ভাড়া আরোপ করিতে বিরত থাকিবে ।

বর্ণিত অবস্থায় দেখা যায় যে, কয়েকটি ক্ষেত্র ব্যতীত অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন, ২০০৩ একটি ন্যায় বিত্তিক আইন ৷ উক্ত আইন ঋণদাতা ও ঋণ গ্রহীতা উভয়পক্ষের অধিকার সংরক্ষণ করে বিধায় এই আইনকে দেশের অর্থনৈতিক শৃৎখলা ও সুশাসন প্রতিষ্ঠার জন্য একটি চমৎকার আইন বলিলে অত্যুক্তি হইবে না ৷

২০ ৷ আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান ও ঋণ গ্রাহকদের যে সকল সুবিধাদি অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন প্রদান করা হইয়াছে তাহা যেমন উভয়পক্ষের মধ্যে সামঞ্জস্যতা রক্ষা সহ আইনের সমতা বিরাজ করে এবং ঋণ আদায়ের ক্ষেত্রেও খুব জোরালো ভূমিকা থাকে কিন্তু কর্পোরেশনের উল্লেখিত বিধান মতে এ ধরনের সুযোগ-সুবিধা এবং ঋণ আদায়ের ক্ষেত্রে সুগঠিত এবং কার্যকরি বিধানের অভাব পরিলক্ষিত হয় । উল্লেখ্য যে যদি কেহ বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং কর্পোরেশনের বাহিরের কোন প্রতিষ্ঠানের নিকট হইতে গৃহঋণ গ্রহণ করেন এবং ঋণ খেলাপী হন তাহা হইলে উক্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানকে বকেয়া ঋণের পর্যাপ্ত উপর Advaluram কের্টি ফি প্রদান সহ আসল টাকার ২০০% (১০০+২০০=৩০০) সুদের ভিতরে প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা করিতে হয় ৷ কিন্তু বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশনের বকেয়া ঋণ আদায়ের ক্ষেত্রে এবং তাহা আমলের ২০০ গুনের বেশী হইলেও শুধুমাত্র ৫ টাকার কোর্ট ফি দিয়া তাহাদের প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা করিতে পারেন, যাহা সংবিধানের প্রদত্ত মৌলিক অধিকারের ২৭ অনুচ্ছেদের চরম লঙ্ঘন এবং যাহার প��িপ্রেক্ষিতে মৌলিক অধিকারের ৩১নং অনুচ্ছেদকেও আঘাত করে ৷ বিষয়টি বিবেচনা এবং অনুধাবনের লক্ষ্যে অনুচ্ছেদদ্বয়ের বক্তব্য নিম্নে অনুলিখন করা হইলঃ

“অনুচ্ছেদ ২৭ ।
সকল নাগরিক আইনের দৃষ্টিতে সমান এবং আইনের সমান আশ্রয় লাভের অধিকারী ।
অনুচ্ছেদ ৩১ I
আইনের আশ্রয় লাভ ও আইন অনুযায়ী ব্যবহার লাভ যে কোন স্থানে অবস্থানরত প্রত্যেক নাগরিকের এবং সাময়িকভাবে বাংলাদেশে অবস্থানরত অপরাপর ব্যক্তির অবিচ্ছেদ্য অধিকার এবং বিশেষতঃ আইন অনুযায়ী ব্যতীত এমন কোন ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা যাইবে না যাহাতে কোন ব্যক্তির জীবন, স্বাধীনতা, দেহ, সুনাম বা সম্পদের হানি ঘটে ।”

২১ ৷ অত্যন্ত পরিতাপের বিষয় দায়িক-আপীলকারীপক্ষ গৃহঋণের জন্য ৭,৭২,০০০/- টাকা গ্রহণ করেন এবং বর্তমানে ডিক্রিদার কর্পোরেশনের দাবী হইতেছে ২৯,৬১,৫৫০.৬০ টাকা ৷ কিন্তু একই ঋণ অন্য কোন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের নিকট হইতে গ্রহণ করিলে দায়িকপক্ষকে যে টাকা পরিশোধ করিতে হইত তাহা বর্তমানে দাবীকৃত টাকার চেয়ে কম । যেখানে দায়িক আপীলকারীদেরকে বাংলাদেশ সংবিধানের প্রদত্ত মৌলিক অধিকার হইতে বঞ্চিত করা হইতেছে ৷ যেখানে ডিক্রিদার কর্পোরেশনের ঋণ আদায়ের পদ্ধতি বা ঋণ আরোপের পদ্ধতি গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সংবিধানের মৌলিক অধিকারকে ক্ষুন্ন করে সেখানে আদেশের উক্ত বিধিবিধানের কার্যকারিতা হারায় ৷ অধিকম্ভ যেহেতু ডিক্রিদার কর্পোরেশন অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের আওতায় প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা করিতে হইবে।

২২ । যদিও অত্র বিবিধ আপীলটিতে আইনের বিধানটিকে চ্যালেঞ্জ করা হয় নাই কিন্তু প্রত্যেক নাগরিকই ন্যায় বিচার (Complete Justice) পাইতে হকদার ৷ মানুষ আদালতের দ্বারস্থ হয় ন্যায় বিচারের প্রত্যাশায় । আইনে বিধান নাই বলিয়া বিচারক তাহার সম্মুখে উপস্থাপিত বিষয়টি ফেরৎ দিতে পারেন না ৷ এককালে আইনে বিধান নাই বলিয়া বিচারক উহা ফেরৎ দিতে পারিতেন । কিন্তু পরবর্তীকালে Equity-র উৎপত্তি হওয়ায় আদালত ন্যায় বিচার প্রতিষ্ঠার লক্ষ্যে equitable principles প্রয়োগ করিয়া বিচারপ্রাথী জনগণকে বিচারের সুফল দিয়া থাকেন । অনেক মামলায় দেখা যায় বন্দী যে প্রতিকার চাহিয়াছে উহা অপ্ৰতুল ৷ তখন আদালত উহার সহজাত ক্ষমতা প্রয়োগ করিয়া প্রার্থীত প্রতিকারকে ফলপ্রসূত (fruitful) করার লক্ষ্যে উহার আনুষঙ্গিক সকল প্রতিকার প্রদান করিয়া থাকেন, ইহা Complete Justice এর জন্যই আদালত করিয়া থাকেন ৷ Complete Justice এর ধারণা এবং উহার পরিব্যপ্তি আলোচনা করিতে গিয়া 20 DLR 320, Arabinda Das Vs. Srinati Sura Das and others মামলায় সিদ্ধান্ত হয় যে,

“The entire body of procedural law is meant for advancement of the cause of justice and not to pose any technical difficulty in the way of the Court to do complete justice between the litigant parties for the administration of which alone it had been created. All technicalities are required to be avoided to secure justice as because end of law is justice.”

২৩ ৷ উপরোক্ত আলোচনা, পর্যালোচনা ও সিদ্ধান্ত সমূহের আলোকে প্ৰতিয়মান যে, বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের ২নং ধারায় যেমন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান হিসাবে গণ্য, তেমনই ২(ক) উপ-ধারা ক্রমিকে আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান হিসাবে অর্থঋণ আদালত অধ্যাদেশ/আইনের জন্মলগ্ন হইতেই অন্তর্ভূক্ত ৷ অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনে বার বার সংশোধন আনায়ন করা হইয়াছে এবং সংশোধনের মুখবন্ধে উল্লেখ আছে, “আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ঋণ আদায়ের জন্য প্রচলিত আইনের অধিকতর সংশোধন ও সংহতকরণ প্রয়োজনীয়; সেহেতু এতদ্বারা নিম্নরুপ আইন করা হইলঃ”

আইন সভা কর্তৃক অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন প্রণয়নের উদ্দেশ্যকে অধিকতর সংহতকরণ তথা কার্যকর করার নিমিত্তে বার বার সংশোধন করা হইয়াছে ৷ তাই আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের ঋণ আদায়ের ক্ষেত্রে অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের মূল উদ্দেশ্যের প্ৰতি সর্বোচ্চ গুরুত্ব বিবেচনায় নেওয়ার দাবী রাখে এবং আইনসভা কর্তৃক অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন প্রণয়নের উদ্দেশ্যও তাহাই ৷ যদিও বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশনের আদেশের বিধানে ঋণ আদায়ের সংক্ষিপ্ত পদ্ধতি সন্নিবেশিত আছে, কিন্তু যখন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের বকেয়া ঋণ আদায়ের জন্য একটি প্রায় পদ্ধতিগত অধিকতর সংহতকরণ ও স্বয়ংসম্পূর্ণ আইন প্রণয়ন হয় এবং উক্ত আইনে বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশনকে আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান হিসাবে অন্তর্ভূক্ত করা হয় তখন উক্ত আদেণের বিশেষ বিধান যাহা ইতোপূর্বে ‘Enactment’ হিসাবে বিবেচিত তাহার কার্যকারিতা হারায় এবং ‘Act’ এর প্রাধান্য প্রতিষ্ঠা পায় ৷ সেই ক্ষেত্রে বলা যায়, বাংলাদেশ হাউস বিল্ডিং ফাইন্যান্স কর্পোরেশন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান হিসাবে অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের আওতাধীন।

২8 ৷ উপরোক্ত আংলাচনা-পর্ষালোচনার পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে অত্র আপীলটি মঞ্জুর করার মত আইনের জোরাল সমর্থন রহিয়াছে বলিয়া আমাদের অভিমত ৷

২৫ ৷ অতএব, ফলাফল; আপীলটি নিম্নলিখিত নির্দেশনাসহ মঞ্জুর করা হইল:-

১ ৷ বিজ্ঞ জেলা ও দায়রা জজ, খুলনা আদালতের দেওয়ানী ১১৪/২০০৬নং ডিক্রিজারী মোকদ্দমায় প্রচারিত ২০/০৭/২০১০ তারিখের আদেশ রদ ও রহিত করা হইল ৷
২ । দায়িক-আপীলকারী ২-৯নং প্রতিপক্ষদের জমাকৃত ৪,৪৮,০০০/- টাকা দরখাস্তকারী-ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষ কর্পোরেশনের সার্কুলার নং ০২/২০০৮ ও ০২/২০০৯ এর পরি-বিধান অনুযায়ী শতকরা ৩০% ভাগ গণক্রমে উল্লেখিত টাকা সমম্বয়পূর্বক যে পাওনা টাকা অবশিষ্ট হ্ইবে, তাহা ১৬৯ঢি কিন্তিতে পরিশোধের নিমিত্তে পুনঃতফসিলীকরণের নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হইল ৷ তবে বকেয়া ঋণ আমলের শতকরা ২০০% (১০০+২০০=৩০০) এর বেশী হইতে পারিবে না।

৩ ৷ অত্র রায় ও আদেশ প্রাপ্তির ০১(এক) মাসের মধ্যে ডিক্রিদার-১নং প্রতিপক্ষকে পূর্ণাঙ্গ হিসাব-নিকাশান্তে কিস্তির টাকা নির্ধারণপূর্বক দায়িকপক্ষকে অবগতি করার পরের মাস হইতে কিন্তি প্রদানের নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হইল ৷ ব্যর্থতায় বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি বিক্রয়ের মাধ্যমে বকেয়া ঋণ সমন্বয় করিতে পারিবে।

২৬ । একই কারণে দেওয়ানী ৫৩০(এফএম)/২০১০নং রুলটি চূড়ান্ত (এ্যাবসলিউট) করা হইল ।

২৭ । রায়ের অনুরিলি অবগতি ও কার্যকর ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের জন্য বিচারিক আদালতে প্রেরণের নির্দেশ দেওয়া হইল I

End.

caseno: Writ Petition No. 3210 of 2001 along with Writ Petition Nos. 7012 of 2003, 1973 of 2005 and 4493 of 2005.
lawyer:
Yousuf Hossain Humayun with JH Afric, Advocates  ------ For the Petitioners in Writ Petition Nos. 3210 0/2001 and 7012 0/2003. 
SM Moonir; Advocate ------ For the Petitioner in Writ Petition No. 1973 0/2005. 
SM Atiqur Rahman" Advocate ------ For the Petitioners in Writ Petition No. 4493 0/2005. 
Mahbubey Alam, Attorney-General, with Biswojit Roy, Deputy Attorney General. 
Amatul Karim, Assistant Attorney-General, "Md Asaduzzaman, Assistant Attorney-General and Shafiqul Islam, Assistant Attorney-General ------ For the Respondents in-(All the Writ Petitions).
parties:
Mangal Chandra Sarker and others  ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Bangladesh and others  ------ Respondents  ------ in all the Writ Petitions
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J : The facts of 4(for) writ petitions being WP Nos. 3210 of 2001; 7012 of 2003; 1973 of 2005 and 4493 of 2005 are identical and they are heard together and disposed of by this judgment.

2. In Writ Petition No. 3210 of 2010 the petitioners challenged the Gazette - Notification dated 15th October, 1974 in respect of the land .of plot Nos. 15,- 35,36, 41, 57, 79 and 84, Gazette Notification dated 24-11-1988 in respect.to the land of plots No. 15, 35,36, 41,79,84 and 117; Gazette Notification dated 21-8-1989 in respect of the land of plot Nos. 84 and 79 and Gazette Notification dated 4th September, 1990 in respect of plot Nos. 17 and 117 by which the Government acquired the aforesaid property of the petitioners situated at Mouza-Chakoli, JL No. 214, Police Station Pallabi, Dhaka (Annexures- 'C', 'D', 'E' and 'F' respectively).

3. In Writ Petition No. 7012 of 2003 the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned notice/order orally published/served upon the petitioner by beating drum on 15-11-2003 asking, the petitioner to vacate the land in question showing the same to be acquired in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 within 7 days should not be declared to have been made illegally and without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. "

4. In Writ Petition No, 1973 9f2005 the petitioners challenged the Gazette Notifications dated 15th October, 1974; 28th, November; 1974; 28th  November, 1980; 24th November,: 1988, 21st August, 1989 and 4th September, 1990 published by the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms by which the Government acquired the property of the petitioners situated at Mouza Chakuli, JL No. 214, Police Station Pallabi, DhaKa (As fully described in paragraph No.9 of the 'writ petition).

5. In Writ Petition No. 449 of 2005 the petitioners challenged the Gazette Notifications dated 15-10-1974; 28-11-1980; 24-11-1988; 21-8-1989 and 4-9-1990 (Annexures- B, B 1; B2, B3 and B4) by which the Government acquired the property of the petitioners situated at District Dhaka, Mouza Chakuli, JL, No, 214, Police Station Pallabi.

6. The facts of all the writ petitions, in short; are that the petitioners were the owners and possessors of the lands as described in the writ petitions. They got those lands by way of inheritance or by purchase from the CS and SA recorded tenants.

7. The Gazette Notifications regarding the acquisition of the lands recorded in plot Nos. 15, 31, 36, 41, 57, 69, 84, 117 and 17 of Mouza Chakuli are the subject matter of writ petition No.3210 of 2001. The notifications regarding the land recorded in CS and SA Plot Nos. 14, 43, 67, 73, 77 and 88 of the same Mouza are the subject matter of writ petition No. 7012 of 2003. The Notifications regarding the land recorded in CS and  SA Plot Nos. 73, 77, 57, 75, 68, 59, 61, 69, 71, 76 and 93 are the subject matter of writ petition No. 1973 of 2005, The Notifications regarding the land recorded in plot Nos. 85, 86, 87, 27, 33, 16, 65, 99, 81, 100, 62, 63, 66, 95, 97, 29, 94 and 98 are the subject matter of writ petition No. 4493 of 2005.

8. The petitioners, have challenged the alleged oral direction of the respondents to the petitioners to vacate the possession of the land described therein in Writ Petition No.7012 of 2003  But it appears to us from, the said petition that the petitioners substantially raised their grievance against the order of-acquisition of the land described therein.

9. The petitioners, in all the writ petitions, narrating their claim of title stated that the respondents did not comply the provisions of relevant law while milking requisition and subsequently acquisition of the land in question. No statutory notices under the provision of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (hereinafter referred as the Act) were served upon the petitioners or their predecessors-in-interest. It has also been stated that the questioned hinds were requisitioned by the Government in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66 and those were subsequently derequisitioned during the pendency of writ petition Nos. 257 to 264, 302 to 311, 326, 327, 329, 339, 340, 343, 360, 370 to 374, 392 and 396 of 1969. The learned Deputy Attorney General for' the Government admitted in those writ petitions that, the lands in question were derequisitioned. Accordingly those rules were dis- charged as prayed for. It has further been stated that the petitioners have been possessing the disputed land. There are mosque, graveyard, temple, etc, in some plots. No compensation was paid to the petitioners on preparing the compensation assessment role.

10. In all the writ petitions the Government appeared and filed affidavits-in-oppositions.

11. The case of the Government, in substance, is that some portions of the lands in question were requisitioned and thereafter acquired by the Government by Gazette notification dated 19-1-1970. Government again requisitioned the said land and other questioned land for acquisition for Jatyo Rakkhi Bahini (including the land which were derequisitioned in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66) and finally acquired in LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 observing all the legal formalities. The notices under the provisions of the Act were served upon the owners and possessors of the said land. Compensation assessment rule was duly prepared and the owners received compensation. The decision of acquisition have been published in the official Gazette. The title and possession of the land in question had been vested in the Government free from all encumbrances. There was no illegality or irregularity in the process of acquisition.

12. Mr. Yousuf Hossain Humayun and Mr. JH Afric, the learned Advocates, appeared on behalf of the petitioners in writ petition Nos. 3210 of 2001 and 7012 of 2003, Mr. SM Moonir, the learned Advocate, appeared on behalf of the petitioners in writ petition No. 1973 of 2005 and Mr. SM Atiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners in writ petition No. 4493 of 2005. On the other hand, Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney General, with Mr. Biswojit Roy, the learned Attorney General, Mr. Amatul Karim, AAG, Mr. Md. Asaduzzaman, AAG, and Mr. Shafiqul Islam, AAG appeared on behalf of the respondents in all the writ petitions.

13. Mr. JH Afric, the learned Advocate, at first, submits that the process of requisition and acquisition of the land in question in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66 is a nullity in view of the fact that the same was not acquired for public purpose. The law did not authorize the respondents to acquire any land other than public purpose. He submits that, in fact, after making de requisition of the land in 1973, the Government left the process of acquisition in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66. The Government gave up their claim in the land after derequisition in 1973 by conduct. He further submits that the order of acquisition in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73, after making de requisition of the said land in 1973, is not permissible in law. He further submits that the original owners of the land including the petitioners had not received any statutory notice as per provisions of the Act. No compensation assessment role was prepared and award was not made in the name of the petitioners or their predecessors-in-interest. The respondents acquired some portion of some plots without any specification which is not permissible in law. He submits that while making such requisition and acquisition the respondents did not consider the hardship of the people who have been possessing the land since the day immemorial.. There are mosque, mandir, graveyard etc. in some portions of the plots. Government cannot take over possession of the said land. He finally submits that since the instant proceeding of requisition and acquisition has not been made in accordance with the provision of Law, the impugned Gazette Notifications are liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

14. Mr. SM Moonir the learned Advocate, drawing our attention to the provisions of sections 3, 4 and 5 of the Act, submits that the procedures as provided in those sections had not been complied. With while making requisition and acquisition of the land in question, He submits, that the said land had been derequisitioned in 1973, After admitting the story of derequisition, the Government is barred by the provision of estoppel to say that the same was not derequisitioned. He submits that from the order sheet of LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 it is apparent that no notice was served upon the owners of the land in question arid no compensation was assessed and paid to them. He submits that onus lies upon the Government to establish that the notice of requisition and acquisition were served duly upon the owners of the land. The proceeding of LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 and the impugned Gazette Notifications are liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

15. Mr. SM Atiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate, adopted the submission as made by Mr. JH Afrie and Mr. SM Moonir.

16. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney General, submits that some portions of the land in question previously were acquired by the Government in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66 for housing scheme and accordingly Gazette Notification was published and after so notification the title and possession of the said land had been vested in the Government. Thereafter, the said land was handed over to Messrs Eastern Housing Ltd. The said portions of the land were again requisitioned for the public purpose in LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 and notice was issued upon the Eastern Housing Ltd. After due compliance of all legal formalities the said land was finally acquired. He submits that some portions of the land were requisitioned in LA Case No, 90 of 1965-66 but those were not acquired, Those lands were released from requisition. Thereafter, again requisitioned in LA Case No.5 of 197-2-73 and finally acquired. Rest of the lands were requisitioned and acquired in the said-LA Case afresh: Notices were duly served and compensation was duly assessed and paid. He submits that there is no illegality and irregularity in the process of requisition and subsequent acquisition. Finally he submits that the Government snail not remove any structure of mosque, mandir etc. and protect the same if it is detected that there are such institutions constructed either before or after acquisition of the questioned land,

17. We have heard the learned Advocates for the petitioners and the learned Attorney General, for the respondents in all the writ petitions, perused the writ petitions, affidavits-in-opposition, affidavits-in-reply and other materials on record.

18. It appears from the rule issuing order and prayer portion of the Writ Petition No. 3210 of 2001 that the petitioners have challenged the Gazette Notifications mentioned above in respect of the land of plot Nos. 15, 35, 36, 41, 57, 79, 84, 117, and 17. The petitioners have instituted the instant writ petition through their constituted power of attorneys, namely MA Awal and Sudhir Chandra Sharke On perusal of the power of attorney (Annexure-A) it appears 'that the petitioners did not execute power in respect of the land recorded in plot No. 57. In that view of the matter our considered opinion is that-the petition in respect of the land recorded in plot 'No. 57 does not deserve any consideration in connection with WP No, 3210 of 2001. Rest of the questioned lands are recorded ill plot Nos. 15, 35, 36, 41, 79, 84, 117 and 17, It appears from Annexure-B to the. Writ Petition No. 3210 of 2001 that the Government .decided to release some plots of different Mouzas from the order of requisition as requisitioned earlier in LA. Case No. 90 of 1965-66 with a view to make requisition and subsequent acquisition for, the scheme of Jatiyo Rakshi Bahini. The description of the land released from the order of requisition in LA Case No.90 of 1965-66 have been given in the schedule which shows that the land measuring an area of 64.1081 acres were released from the order of requisition from Mouza Digun and 0.77 acre of land of plot Nos. 62, 63, 64, 65 and 120 of Mouza Chakuli on 17-8-1973. On 24-8-1973, the land covering 14.70 acres were released from the, order of requisition from Digun Mouza. Thereafter, on 8-9- 1973 the land measuring an area of 27.7431 acres of different plots including plot Nos. 14, 17, 27, 33, 57, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 75, 77, 79, 85, 87, 95, 97 and 117 (questioned in these writ petitions) of Chakuli Mouza were released from requisition. It furthers appears that 130.7050 acres of land of Mouza Senpara Parbata, again 158.4481 acres of land of Mouza Senpara Parbata, 92.1684 acres of land of Baunia Mouza, 24.2717 acres of land of Mouza Digun, 12.96 acres of land of Mouza Merul, 1:42 acres of land of Mouza Senpara Parbata, 3 :03 acres on and of Mouza Chadogan and 49.1736 acres of land of Mouza Duaripara were released on different dates. That is, a total area of 290.3509 acres of land were released from the order of requisition. Out of those lands only 0.10 acre out of 0.40 acre of plot No. 17,0.77 acre of land out of 9.52 acres of plot No. 79,0.19 acre of land out. of 1.96 acres of plot No. 117) the subject matters of WP No.3210 of 2001) were released from, requisition as it appears from the order sheet of LA Case No.90 of 1965-66 produced by the writ petitioner of writ petition No. 3210 of 2001. It further appears from Arinexure-H (Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970) filed by the writ petitioners of WP No. 3210 of 2001 in their epoxy to the affidavit-in-opposition that some of the lands it question were acquired by the Government. The said Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970 shows that those lands were requisitioned on 31st May, 1966. The entire lands of plot Nos. 15, 35, 36 and 41 and part of plot Nos. 57, 79, 84 and 117 were acquired by the said Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970. It has been submitted that the acquisition of land in the Case No. 90 of 1965-66 was not done for public purpose and legal process was not followed. it appears from the writ petitions that the petitioners did not challenge the legality and propriety of the process of requisition and acquisition in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66. So it difficult for us to consider the submission of the 'learned Advocates in these petitions at this stage.

19. The learned Advocates, appearing for the petitioners in WP No. 3210 of 2010, submits that in fact, after releasing the land in question from requisition, the Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970 became mere paper transaction. But on perusal of the order sheet of LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66 produced by the petitioners, (Annexure-B to the Writ Petition No.3210 of 2001) it appears that only' in respect of some portions of the land of disputed plot Nos.17,79 and 117 of WP No. 3210 of 2001 had been released from the order of requisition for the purpose" of acquiring the same for Jatya Rakshi Bahini, 'There' is nothing in Annexure-B that the entire land of the questioned plot Nos. 15,35,36,41 and part of the lands questioned of plot No. 57, 79, 84 and If 7 (except the land covering 0,77 acre out of 9.52 acres of plot No. 79,0.19 acre out of 1.96 acres of plot No. 117 and 0.10 acre out of plot No. 17) had been released from the requisition, 0.77 acres of land from plot No. 79, 0.19 acre from plot No. 117 and 0.10 acre of plot No.17 were released since those lands were not acquired by Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970. Rest is lands which are also subject matter of this writ petition that is, entire land of plots No. 15,35,36 and 41 and part of plot Nos. 79, 84, 17 and 117 were not released from requisition since those lands were finally acquired by Gazette Notification dated 19-7-1970. In absence of any material before us that after publication of the Gazette Notification" on 19-1-1970 (Annexure-H) regarding acquisition of the land of plot Nos. 15,35, 36 and 84 and the I? Art of plot Nos. 57, 79, 84, 117 and 17 the same had been released from acquisition it is difficult for us to accept the submission of the learned Advocate that the land acquired had been released from requisition .and acquisition. The Government is lawfully authorised to withdraw or release any land from the, acquisition before the payment of compensation and order of withdrawal or release must be published in the official Gazette but no such Gazette Notification has been produced before this Court, for consideration. After payment of compensation and publication regarding acquisitioning in official Gazette, the ‘title or the land be vested in the Movement free from and encumbrances and the law does not allow the Government to release the same at that stage. In the case of Bangladesh vs Commercial Trust of Bangladesh Ltd. 46 DLR (AD) 89 it has been held that after payment of compensation for acquisition of land no order can be made for derequisition of such acquired land. Similar view has been taken in the case of Sayed a Hossain vs Wega Fashion Sweater (Pvt) Limited 59 DLR (AD) 83 wherein it has been observed by their Lordships that there is no law authorising the Government to release any land once it .is vested in the Government by acquisition according to law.

20. It appears from the Writ Petition No. 7012 of 2003 that the petitioners of that writ petition, in fact, challenged the order of acquisition of land of plot Nos. 14, 43, 67,73,77 and 88 in the cover to protect their alleged possession stating that the respondents took an attempt to evict them serving oral notice by beating drum. The petitioners claimed 52 acre of land from plot Nos. 14 and 43, 0.43 acre of from plot No. 67, 0.06 acre from plot No. 73 (wherein it is claimed that there is a Mandir) 111 acres of land from plot No. 77 and 1.35 acres of land from plot Note 88. It appears from the Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970 that the entire land of plot No. 43 and the part of the land of plot Nos. 67, 73, 77 and 88 were acquired by the Government. From Annexure-B to the writ petition No. 3210 of 2001 it appears that the rest. Lands, which were not acquired, of plot Nos. 14, 67, 77 had been released from the order of requisition, The said released land was subsequently requisitioned and finally acquired in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 and notified in the official Gazette under section 5(7) of the Act. After so acquisition of the title of the petitioner had been extinguished and the same' was vested in the Government.

21. In Writ Petition No. 1973 of 2005 petitioners claimed the land recorded in plot Nos. 73, 77, 57, 75,68,59,61,69, 71, 76 and 93. From the Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970 it appears that the entire land of plot Nos. 59, 61, 69, 71, 76 and 93 and part of the land of plot Nos. 73, 77 and 57 were acquired by the Government. It appears from order sheet of LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66 that entire land of plot Nos. 68 and 75 (which were not acquired on 19-1-1970) and part of plot Nos. 57 and 77 were released from the order of requisition, i.e., the lands which had been acquired in 1970 had not been derequisitioned or released in 1973. The lands requisitioned, which were not acquired in 1970, had been released in 1973 from requisition. The lands, which were acquired on 19-1-1970 and. the land which were requisitioned and subsequently derequisitioned, were, again requisitioned and thereafter acquired for public purpose in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 and finally published in the impugned Gazette Notifications.

22. Writ Petition No. 4493 of 2005 is related to the lands of plot Nos. 85, 86, 87, 27, 33, 16, 65, 99, 81, 100, 62, 63, 66, 95, 97, 29, 94, and 98. It appears from the Gazette Notification dated 19-1- 1970 that the entire lands of plot Nos. 99, 81, 100, 29, 94 and 98 and part of plot Nos. 65 and 63 Were acquired. From the order sheet of LA Case No.90 of 1965-66 it appears that the entire lands of plot No. 85,87,27,33,62,95,97 and part of plot No. 65 and 63 had been released from requisition those land were not acquired. The lands which were acquired in 1970 and the lands derequisitioned and some other lands were again requisitioned and finally acquired in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 which have been published, in the impugned Gazette Notifications.

23. Now we shall consider the legality 'and propriety of the proceeding of LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73. It appears from the order dated: 1 0-11-1972 of LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 (Annexure-5 series to the Supplementary affidavit in opposition in WP No. 3210 of 2001) that the land of plot Nos. 15, 29, 35, 36, 41, 59, 61, 69, 71, 76, 81, 93, 94, 98, 99, 100 and part of the plot Nos. 14,57,63,65,67, 73, 77, 78, 79, 84 and 117 of Chakuli Mouza were requisitioned by the said order. From the Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970 (Annexure-H to the affidavit in reply filed in W. 3210 of 2001) it appears that the lands of those plots were first requisitioned on 31st May 1966 and acquired by the said notification dated 19-1-1970. Thereby the title of those lands were vested in the Government: It is evident that requiring body was Messrs Eastern Housing Limited. From the orders of derequisition of LA Case No.5 of 1977-73 it appears that the land acquired and handed over to Messrs Eastern Housing Ltd had again been requisitioned for the purpose of acquisition. It was directed to publish the order of requisition in Tahshilders and village Panchayet's office of the locality and the contents of the order was to be published by beating of drum in the locality. It was argued by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the notice of the said order of requisition and subsequent acquisition had not been served upon the petitioners. Since the land as mentioned above had been acquired in 1970 by way of Gazette Notification and title of the same was vested to the Eastern Housing Ltd. through Government as per provision of section 5(7) of the Act, so service of notice to the petitioners for those portions of questioned land does not arise at all. It appears from page 133 of the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition filed in Writ Petition No. 3210 of 2001 that 'notice under section 3 of the Act was issued upon the Eastern Housing Ltd. in respect of the land of the plot as mentioned above and the some other plots and same was accepted on behalf of the Eastern Housing Ltd. It further appears from the order dated 11-11-1972 (page 17) that after assessment of the compensation the cheques were issued in favour of the Managing Director of Eastern Housing Ltd. Finally order of acquisition was published, in the impugned Gazette Notification dated 15-10-1974. From Annexure-D to the WP No. 3210 of 2001 it appears that the possession of the land as acquired was resumed by the Government by another impugned notification dated 13-11-1988. Annexure- D is the Notification regarding resumption of possession of the land acquired by notification dated 15-10-1974 but the petitioners of WP No. 3210 of 2001 have challenged the said notification terming the same as Notification regarding acquisition.

24. From the order dated 20-8-1973 passed in LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 it transpires that some portion of the plots 62, 63 and 65 of Mouza Chakuli (subject matter of WP No. 4493 of 2005) were requisitioned by the Government. Owners were directed to make over possession of those land. It was directed to publish the copy of the order of requisition to Tahshilder's office, village Panchayet's office and by beat of drum in the locality. Nazir was directed to cause service of the notice.

25.  From the order dated 10-9-1973 of LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 it appears that the, land of questioned plot Nos. 14, 17, 27, 33, 57, 62, 63, 65, 66,68, 75, 77, 79, 85, 87, 95, 97 and 117 of Mouza Chakuli were requisitioned. Similarly it was directed to publish notice to TahshiIders and village Panchayet's office and by beating drum in the locality: Nazir was directed to cause service of notice and to put up the service return. On, the same date notices under Section 5(1)(a) and 5(3) of Act were signed by Land Acquisition Officer and Nazir was again directed to cause service. It appears from the second order dated 10-9-1973 that the Kanongo assessed the compensation of a sum of Taka 48, 24, 272.52. Accordingly, after so assessment notice under sections 5(1)(a) and 5(3) of the Act were issued. It appears from the subsequent orders that one Wazedul Islam claiming himself the power of attorney of the persons against whom the compensation was awarded made an attempt to get the compensation but the authority concerned directed the office to verify the genuineness of such claim and after verification of the said power of attorney the said amount was paid to those persons. Thereafter, some other persons withdrew the money of compensation. It has been argued by Mr Afric that the said compensation was not actually paid to the owners of the land in question. If any such grievance is there the aggrieved person may take legal step in Civil Court in a competent suit. In this writ jurisdiction it is difficult for us to consider the submission as made by Mr Afric.

26. The grievance of the learned Advocates for the petitioners is that no notice was served upon the original owners of the land in question. It appears from the order dated 7-11-1973/8-11-1973 (relevant page 78 of Supplementary affidavit in opposition of WP No. 3210 of 2001) that the land owners filed an objection before the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reform. Consequently the proceeding was stayed. That is they were aware about the proceeding.

27. It further appears from certificate of possession that Requiring Body (page 97), that is, the Housing and Settlement Department, took over possession of some land of .questioned plots namely Plot Nos. 14, 17,27, 33, 57, 62, 63, 65, 66, 65, 68, 73,75, 77, 79, 85, 87, 95, 97 and 117 from Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka, on 28-11-1973. It also transpires from the certificate of possession' (Page 103) that the Requiring Body took over possession of the entire lands of questioned plot Nos. 15, 29, 35,36,41,43,59,61,69,71,76,77,93,94,98,99 and 100 and part of questioned plot Nos. 14, 57, 63, 65; 67, 73, 77, 79,84,88 and 117 of Mouza Chakuli from the Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka.

28. The learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners emphatically argued that no notice under section 1 I think it will be 5(1a) has been served upon the petitioners or their predecessors-in-interest but it appears from page 125 to the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition that the notices under the provision of section 1 I think it will be 5(1a) of the Act, which is a public notice to be given at the convenient places or near the property proposed to be acquired, were served. It appears that the notices under section 1 I think it will be 5(1 a) of the Act in respect of entire land of questioned plot Nos. 15, 29, 32, 35, 36, 41, 43, 59, 61, 66, 69, 71, 76, 93, 94, 98, 99, 100 and part of questioned plot Nos. 14, 57, 63, 65, 66, 67, 73, 77, 79, 84 and 117 of Chakuli Mouza had been issued to serve by hanging in the Notice Boards of the office of Chairman, Hari Rampur Union Council, Mirpur, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the Police Station, Mirpur, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the Sub-Registrar, Kalabagan, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the LA Collector, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the DC, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the District Judge, Dhaka, Notice Board of the office of the Commissioner Dhaka Division, Dhaka, Notice Board of the Municipality, Dhaka, and the Notice Board of the Revenue Circle Officer, Mirpur, Dhaka. In such view of the matter it is difficult to accept the sub- mission of the learned Advocates for the petitioners that the notice under section II think it will be 5(1 a) had not been served in accordance 'with law. From the order dated 28-11-1988 it appears that some papers relating requisition and acquisition of land in LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 were called for by the Anti-Corruption Officer and those papers were found to be untraced.

29. In the case of Bangladesh vs Fazle Karim reported in 42 DLR (AD) 91, it has been observed by their Lordships of the Appellate Division that the presumption of service of public notice for acquisition of property being an official act, a presumption is available under the Evidence Act that it has been regularly performed unless the country is proved. Section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, provided that the Court may presume that the judicial and official acts have been regularly performed. Where once making to an order under a statute has been proved, there may well be presumption that it was duly made as required by law. Once the publications of the orders in the official Gazette are established the process of publications should be presumed to have been considered sufficient. Since the proceedings took place long ago the same must be presumed to be regular. Similarly, where the report states that symbolical possession is delivered, there is a presumption as to formalities having been complied with. Irregularity is not to be presumed, but a party alleging it may prove it. The writ petitioners did not take any step to rebut the presumption.

30. In view of the facts and circumstances as mentioned above it is difficult for us to accept the submissions of the learned Advocates for the petitioners that no notice was issued or served or no compensation was paid to the original owners to the land in question.

31. If there be any grievance of the petitioners about non-payment of compensation they may make their grievance before the competent Court of law.

32. In the case of Abdullah-al-Mamun vs Secretary, Ministry of Land and others, reported in 10 BLC (AD) 105, it transpires that alleging legality and propriety of proceeding of LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 in respect of Chakuli Mouza and some other Mouzas a writ petition was filed and rule was issued and ultimately that rule was discharged against which the petitioners preferred Leave Petition in the Appellate Division and their Lordships of the Appellate Division quoted the following portion of the Judgment of the High Court Division:

“She further submits that according to the plaintiff the properties appertain to the waft estate while the Government claims that it does not from part of the waif estate so, it is a disputed question of fact, which can only be resolved by a civil Court of competent jurisdiction and that suit at the instance of the writ petitioner is still pending and, as such, Rule should be discharged on that account. She further submits that there is no legal bar for fresh requisition for a public purpose of any property which was previously derequisitioned and that notices under section 5(7) having been published as evidence from Annexures-B-B(l) to the writ petition as well as by Annexures 1, 2 and 3 respectively to the affidavit-in-opposition the land in question has absolutely vested in the Government free from all encumbrances and that full compensation has been paid to the normal owners and accordingly, there is no scope for withdrawing from the requisition inasmuch as section 8(B) of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 provides that the Government may withdraw from the process of requisition before compensation is paid and has relief on the case of Abdul Mannan vs Ministry of Land Administration 27 DLR 297 and then their Lordships have observed,

"It appears that the High Court Division, considered the plea as to the question of wagestate and the High Court Division answered the question as under (quoted above)

In view of the above, we do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioner."

33. That is their Lordships did not find any illegality in finding of the High Court Division that there is no legal bar for fresh requisition for a public purpose of any property which was previously derequisitioned. Since the aforesaid Judgment delivered by their Lordships of the Appellate Division regarding the act of acquisition of the land in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 the same is binding upon this Division.

34. Here, in the instant petitions it appears to us that some portions of the land were acquired and decision of acquisition was published in the official Gazette on 15-10-1970 under section 5(7) of the Act. The title and possession of those lands were vested in the Government who delivered possessions to the requiring body. Those lands were again requisitioned in LA Case No.5 of 1972-75 and after service of necessary notices and payment of compensation to the said requiring body those lands were again acquired. Some portions of the questioned land were earlier requisitioned but not acquired at the time. Those land were derequisitioned from the proceeding of LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66. Those were again requisitioned and finally acquired in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73. Rest of the lands were requisitioned and thereafter acquired in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 afresh. After publication of notices in the official Gazette under Section 5(7) of the Act the title and possession of those lands have been vested in the Government free from all encumbrances. Challenge of the notifications as to acquisition of the lands in question published in the Official Gazette on 15-10-1975, 24-11-1988,20-8-1989, 4-9-1990, 28-11-1980 after long lapse of time on the plea of non-services of notices does not deserve any consideration in this summary proceeding. Whether the petitioners had received notices of requisition and acquisition or not is essentially a disputed question of fact which cannot be resolved in writ petition.

<u>35. Mr Afric relied on the case of the province of East Pakistan vs Jogesh Chandra Lodh, 11 DLR SC 11 wherein it has been observed that where the officer concerned did not apply his mind to the question the requisition order is invalid. That petition was filed before acquisition, challenging the order of requisition. Similarly case cited by Mr Afric reported in 15 DLR page 453 (Herama Chandra Battacharjee vs The Secretary, Department of Revenue and others the petitioner challenged order of derequisition The citations have got no manner of application in the present case, In the case of Bangladesh vs Nabab Abdul Malik Jute Mills Ltd. reported in 60 DLR(AD) 7 it has been observed by their Lordships of the Appellate Division that once the property is acquired and Gazette Notification is published under section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of the Property Act; the fight, title and ,interest, if any, of the owners are extinguished and preparation of Khatian and payment of rent does not improve the position of the original owner in respect of acquired land.</u>

36. The learned Attorney General assured all concerned on behalf of the Government that if it detected that there are mosque, Mandir and graveyard, in any portion of the amid in question the Government will not take any step to demolish the same. We hope that the assurance as given by the learned Attorney General would be maintained strictly.

37. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances we do not find any substance in the Rules.

38. In the result the Rules in Writ Petition Nos. 3210 of 2001, 7012 of 2003, 1973 of 2005 and 4493 of 2005 are hereby discharged. The orders of status quo granted earlier are hereby recalled and vacated.

39. At this stage, the learned Advocates for the petitioners pray sometimes to remove the home steads of the petitioners allegedly situated in some portions of the land in question. If it is detected that there are homesteads of the petitioners in any portion of the questioned land the respondents may allow 3 months’ time to remove their homesteads from the places wherein their homesteads are situated considering their humanitarian approach,

Communicate the order at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 665 of 2009.
lawyer:
Karunamoy Chakma, Deputy Attorney-General, instructed by Gias Uddin Ahmed, Advocate-on-Record- (From the judgment and order dated the 28th January of 2009 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in Administrative Appellate Tribunal Miscellaneous Case NO.OI of 2009) ----- For the Petitioners. 
None represented ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh and others -----Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Nurul Alam ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 28th January of 2009 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in Administrative Appellate Tribunal Miscellaneous Case No. 01 of 2009)
full_judgment:
Md A Wahhab Miah J:The petitioners, the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and the other Government functionaries have filed this petition against the order dated 28-1-2009 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in Miscellaneous Case No. 01 of 2009 dismissing the same.

2. At the very outset, we cannot help ourselves but to say that the leave petition has been filed in a careless manner without giving minimum facts to have the background in filing the same. However, from the impugned order and the other materials, such as, the order passed by the Administrative Tribunal in the Administrative Tribunal case, the Memorandum of Appeal of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal Appeal No.235 of 2005 filed before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, we have gathered facts which are as follows:

3. The sole respondent as petitioner filed Administrative Tribunal Case No.295 of 1999 before Administrative Tribunal No.3, Dhaka against the order dated 09-5-1999 passed by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, rejecting his appeal filed against the order dated 29-09-1998 imposing a major penalty upon him by degrading him to the time scale, i.e. below his salary scale (তাহার বেতন স্কেলের নিম্ন টাইম স্কেল)for 2 (two) years under rule (4) (3) (a) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 (the Rules, 1985). Subsequently, the case was renumbered as Administrative Tribunal Case No.161 of 2003.

4. The Administrative Tribunal after hearing the parties by order dated 22-09-2005 allowed the case in part by imposing minor penalty, i.e. withholding the annual increment of the petitioner for two years under rule 4(2)(b) of the Rules, 1985, instead of major penalty awarded by the department.

5. Against the said order of the Administrative Tribunal, the present petitioners who were respondents filed Administrative Appellate Tribunal Appeal No.230 of 2005 before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka. 11-06-2006 was fixed in the appeal for filing paper book; it was not filed and tile appeal was dismissed for such default. Thereafter an application was filed by the present petitioners on 05-01-2009, after about 6(six) months of the said order of dismissal for restoration of the appeal. The application was registered as AAT Miscellaneous Case No. 01 of 2009. By the impugned order, the Appellate Tribunal dismissed the miscellaneous case on the ground of limitation; hence this petition for leave to appeal.

6. The relevant portion of the order of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal reads as follows:-

"There is no mention of limitation in the Administrative Tribunal Rules, 1982 of filing an application for restoration of a case, dismissed on default. But the Administrative Appellate Tribunal has fixed a period of maximum. 90 days for filing the application for restoration in the AAT Misc. Case No.3/1999 and still then the practice is going on.

The present application for restoration has been filed on 05-01-2008 about 6 months after the order issued by these(sic)Tribunal. As the application has been made beyond 90 days, the limitation period fixed and practised in this Tribunal, we are not inclined to accept the application. "

7. In the above backdrop, the points to be decided in this petition are: (a) whether an appeal filed before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal could be dismissed for default for non-filing of paper book, (b) whether any limitation has been prescribed in the relevant laws, namely: the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 (the Act, 1980) and the Rules, 1982 for filing an application for restoration of an appeal dismissed for default and lastly (c) whether the Administrative Appellate Tribunal was justified in .dismissing the miscellaneous case on the ground that the same was filed beyond 90 days relying on an earlier decision by it in another case.

8. Mr. Karunamoy Chakma, learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing for the petitioners, has candidly submitted that he personally went to the office of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal to obtain a copy of the order passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal : in "AAT Misc. Case No.3/1999" relying on which 'the Administrative Appellate Tribunal passed the impugned order dismissing the miscellaneous case in question and thus, rejected the application for restoration of Administrative Appellate Tribunal (AAT) Appeal No.235 of 2005 on the ground that the same was filed beyond 90 days which period was fixed in the said AAT miscellaneous case for filing an application for restoration. But he found that no such order was passed in "AAT Misc. Case No. 3/1999", he could trace that in fact, it is Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 1998 in which the Administrative Appellate Tribunal allowed 90(ninety) days time to the appellant for filing an application for restoration of an administrative tribunal case which was rejected by the Tribunal as being barred by limitation as the same was filed beyond 30(thirty) days and so far as he could ascertain that order (the order passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 1998) being followed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in considering the merit of an application for restoration and in the instant case, the Administrative Appellate Tribunal also followed the order made in the said appeal, but as a typing mistake instead of appeal, it was written as case and the year was also written wrongly as 1999 in place of 1998. The learned Deputy Attorney-General produced the certified copy of the order passed in the said Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 1998.

9.The learned Deputy Attorney-General has further submitted that allowing 90(ninety) days time for filing an application for restoration of an administrative tribunal case or appeal, as the case may be, is contrary to the provisions of the Rules, 1982. Moreso, allowing of a period in the given facts and circumstances of that particular case cannot be the basis for deciding the fate of other cases. Therefore, the Appellate Tribunal erred in law in rejecting the application for restoration of the appeal by the impugned order by making a reference to the decision given in an earlier case and, as such, the same calls for interference by this Division. In support of his submission, the learned Deputy Attorney- General has referred to a decision of this Division given in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs. Md. Abdul Karim (CP No. 43 of 2010).

10. From the certified copy of the order passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 1998, it appears that in the said appeal period of 90 days was allowed to the appellant for filing the application for restoration for that case only. In the said appeal, the Appellate Tribunal observed that:-

"The learned Advocates have drawn our attention to the proviso to section 7 of the Act to the effect that where in respect of any matter no procedure has been prescribed by this Act or by rules made there under, a Tribunal shall follow such procedure in respect of thereof as may be laid down by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal. It is submitted on behalf of the Bar that this Tribunal may prescribe a time limit for such an application."

11. It is necessary to state that the miscellaneous appeal arose out of an order passed by the Administrative Tribunal, dismissing Miscellaneous Case No.54 of 2996 as being barred by limitation, the same having been filed beyond 30(thirty) days. (the application was filed for restoration of the Administrative Tribunal case which was dismissed for default).

12. The Appellate Tribunal further observed in the said miscellaneous appeal that:

"We think, on the analogy of the relevant provisions in the Code a period of 30 days is quite reasonable for the purpose. But since there has been no law on the subject at the time of filing of the instant application, the applicant cannot be surprised be (sic) taking him to task for not coming within 30 days. In absence of a fixed period, the period less than 90 days taken by the applicant made without sufficient cause cannot be treated as quite reasonable, although we must not be understood to be saying that in future applications such relaxation would be permissible. In such view of the matter, the application cannot be treated as time barred."

13. It appears to us that in not treating the application for restoration as being time barred in Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 1998 on the observations as quoted herein before, the Administrative Appellate Tribunal totally failed to consider sub-rule (7) of rule 6 read with rule II of the Rules, 1982. Sub-rule (7) of rule 6 has specifically dealt with the filing of application for restoration of an appeal dismissed for default-or for setting-aside an ex-parte order either by the Administrative Tribunal or by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal and in sub-rule (7) no time limit has been prescribed for filing such applications. Sub-rule (7) has empowered the Tribunals to make an order setting-aside the dismissal or the order made ex-parte on such conditions as it deems fit subject to its satisfaction that "there was sufficient cause for the non-appearance of the party" on the date fixed for hearing of the case/appeal. Therefore, it was not at all necessary to prescribe any period of limitation for filing an application for restoration.

14. From a combined reading of sub-rules (4), (5), (6) and (7) of rule 6 of the Rules, 1982, it appears to us that the rule making authority did not think it wise to prescribe any period for tiling an application for restoration of a case or appeal, as the case may be, and left the matter to the satisfaction of the concerned Tribunal whether there was sufficient cause for the non-appearance of the party on the date fixed for hearing in allowing an application for restoration or setting-aside an ex-parte order. But the Administrative Appellate Tribunal failed to consider the said sub-rules in its proper perspective. In view of the language of sub-rule (7) of rule 6 of the Rules, 1982, prescribing a period for filing an application for restoration of a case or appeal either within 30(thirty) days or 90(ninety) days would amount to amending sub-rule (7) of the Rules, 1982 which is the domain of the Government. It also appears that the Appellate Tribunal itself was not sure as to the period to be fixed for filing an application for restoration of a case dismissed for default, when it said in Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 1998 that "a period of 30 days is quite reasonable for the purpose" and then said "In absence of a fixed period the period less than 90 days taken by the applicant made without sufficient cause be treated as quite reasonable, although we must not be understood to be saying that in future applications such relaxation shall be permissible. "

15. Reading the order as a whole passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 1998, it further appears to us that in fact, in the said case, no specific period was prescribed for filing an application for restoration of a case or appeal or for setting-aside an ex-parte order passed in a case or appeal, as the case may be, for the future cases, either for itself or for the Administrative Tribunal, but the period of 90 days was considered as quite reasonable for that particular case only. So, the order passed in the said miscellaneous appeal could not in any way be followed as precedence for the future cases as has been done in the instant case. The point at issue was considered in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.43 of 2010. In the said case after considering the relevant provisions of the Act, 1980, namely: sections 5, 6 and 12 and rules, 6 and 11 of the Rules, 1982, this Division held that:-

"From a close study of the above mentioned provisions of the Act as well as the Rules, it appears to us that no period has been prescribed for filing an application for setting- aside an order of dismissal of an appeal, so the question of rejection of an application on the ground of limitation does not arise at all. But, unfortunately the Administrative Appellate Tribunal has failed to consider this legal aspect of the case in passing the impugned order. The Appellate Tribunal has also not stated the provisions of law under which the appellant was required to file an application for restoration within a specified time when it mentioned that the application was filed out of time by 7 (seven) days. What appears to us is that an Administrative Tribunal or the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, as the case may be, may reject an application for setting-aside an order of dismissal or an ex-parte order even if the same is filed within the shortest possible period, if the applicant or the appellant fails to give sufficient cause to the satisfaction of the concerned Tribunal for failure to appear when the case or appeal was taken up for hearing."

<u>16. We find no reason to take a different view in this case other than the view taken in the said decided case. However, we feel it necessary to add in this case that an application for restoration of an administrative tribunal case or an administrative appellate tribunal appeal or for setting-aside an ex-parte order made by the Tribunals, as the case may be, may be filed even after long gap, but fate of such application would depend upon the satisfaction of the Tribunals as to the sufficiency of the cause filed for such purposes.</u>

17. In conclusion, we hold that the Appellate Tribunal erred in law in dismissing the miscellaneous case in question on the ground that the same was filed beyond 90 (ninety) days without disposing of the application on merit in the light of sub-rule (7) read with sub-rules (4), (5) and (6) of rule 6 of the Rules, 1982.

18. In this case, there is another new dimension, i.e. the appeal for the restoration of which application was filed was dismissed for non-filing of paper book. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has submitted that so far as he could ascertain from the office of the Appellate Tribunal there is no written decision or direction by it to file paper book; the system of filing paper book in the appeal is being followed on the verbal instruction of the Appellate Tribunal given long before when DM Ansaruddin, J was its Chairman, and adhering to such practice, the appeal was dismissed for non-filing of the paper book. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has insisted that the procedure adopted by the Appellate Tribunal is wrong inasmuch as, it has no backing of law and the appeal was dismissed illegally and therefore, the Appellate Tribunal ought to have restored the appeal.

<u>19. The procedure as to the hearing of an appeal by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal is same as that of a case by an Administrative Tribunal. In this regard, it is necessary to state that pursuant to the provisions of section 12 of the Act, 1980 the Government made the Rules, 1982. In the Rules, 1982, detailed provisions have been made as to how an application shall be filed before the Administrative Tribunal registered and disposed of by it including the provisions for restoration in case an application is dismissed for default and to set-aside an order made ex-parte. In the Rules, 1982, no separate procedure has been provided for in respect of filing of an appeal before the Appellate Tribunal, its registration and disposal. Rule 11 of the Rules, 1982, has provided that the provisions of the Rules, 1982 shall, mutatis mutandis, apply to an appeal to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal. And rule 6 of the Rules, 1982 has clearly provided the procedure for disposal of an application. And as per sub-rules (4), (5) and (6) of rule 6 of the Rules, 1982, an application (here the appeal) can be dismissed for default only if on the date fixed for hearing, the applicant does not appear. It is true that proviso to sub-section (8) of section 7 of the Act (in the order passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 1998 it has wrongly been mentioned as proviso to section 7 of the Act) has provided that where, in respect of any matter, no procedure has been prescribed by the Act or by the Rules made there under, a Tribunal shall follow the procedure in respect thereof as may be laid down by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal but when in the Rules, 1982 it has been clearly stated that an application (here the appeal) may be dismissed only when the applicant (here the appellant) does not appear on the date of hearing, then how an appeal could be dismissed for default for non-filing of paper book and that too on the verbal instructions of the Appellate Tribunal as submitted by the learned Deputy Attorney-General. It is true, the Appellate Tribunal can very well prescribe a procedure to be followed by itself or by the Tribunal which has not been provided the Act and the Rules but not contrary to the provisions of the Act, 1980 or the Rules, 1982. And the procedure so prescribed must be made public in writing so that the litigant people can know the consequence of non-compliance of such procedure, but in no case can make a provision for dismissal of a case or appeal for non-compliance of a procedure prescribed by it. Therefore, the order passed by the Appellate Tribunal in dismissing the appeal for non-filing of the paper book also appears to us contrary to the Rules, 1982.</u>

20. Be that as it may, since the Appellate Tribunal dismissed the miscellaneous case in question on the ground that the same was filed "beyond 90 days, the limitation period fixed and practiced in this Tribunal" without considering the explanation given in the application for restoration and the merit of the application, we see no other way but to send back the miscellaneous case on remand to it for disposal on merit in the light of the observations made and the findings given herein before. Accordingly, this leave petition is disposed of in the following terms:

The impugned order dated 28-1-2009 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in AAT Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 2009 is set-aside and the case is sent back on remand to it for hearing afresh and to dispose of the same on merit in the light of the observations made and the findings given hereinbefore.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 896 of 2009
lawyer:
Nahid Mahtab, Advocate instructed by Chowdhury Md Zahangir; Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
None Represented ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
JMS Glass Industries Ltd  ------ Petitioner 
Vs.
Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated the 25th day of November, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 4535, 4105, 4433, 4434, 4435, 4436, 4437, 3523 and 2342 of 2007).
full_judgment:
MA Wahhab Miah J: This petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and Order dated the 25th November, 2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3523 of 2007 discharging the Rule.

2. The petitioner filed the said writ petition before the High Court Division challenging the Order dated 15-3-2007 communicated under Nothi  No. CEVT/ Case (VAT)-192/2006/667 (1) (Annexure 'G' to the writ petition) passed by respondent No.1, Customs,  Excise & VAT, appellate Tribunal, directing it to submit the copy of the treasury chalan after depositing the demanded Value Added Tax (VAT) as per the provisions of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991 (the VAT Act) to have been issued with- out lawful authority and is of no legal effect, Accordingly, the Rule was issued.

3. The case of the writ-petitioner as made out in the writ petition was that respondent No.3, Assistant Commissioner of Customs, Excise & VAT, Siddirganj Division, Narayanganj served a show cause notice upon it bearing Nothi No. 3/A(340) onion/JMS Glass/2005/ 1907 (5-1), dated 23-10- 2005 demanding Taka 3,03,67,190.10 as VAT under section 55 of the VAT Act, alleging evasion for the period between 1-1-1998 to 31-12-2004. The petitioner gave reply to the show cause notice on 28-11- 2005 and claimed that the demand was not in conformity with the actual facts and circumstances and the valid. evidence. The petitioner in support of its reply furnished particulars of relevant documents and claimed that the demand notice was not tenable. The matter was adjudicated upon by respondent No. 3 without considering all the evidence and documents 'produced by the petitioner. The respondent did' not hold. Any Enquiry and took into account only three bill of entries and passed the Order bearing Nothi No. 4/A(340) oniom/JMS Glass/2005/986 (5)-3', dated 29-6-2006 .deducting Taka 5,22,489.43 from the demanded amount of Taka 3,03,67,190.10. The respondent arbitrarily demanded Taka 2,98,44,700.67 and imposed penalty of Taka 3,00,00,000. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the Order of adjudication, the petitioner filed an Appeal to respondent: No, 2, Commissioner (Appeal) on 27-9-2006 mentioning in detail of the documentary evidence and prayed for accepting the Appeal after holding impartial Enquiry, It was further prayed "to grant the Appeal for hearing by waiving deposit of 10%" of the demanded VAT or imposed penalty under section 42 of the VAT Act read with section 196 and proviso to section 194 of the Customs Act, 1969 (The Customs Act). But the respondent, without holding any Enquiry and giving opportunity of hearing the Appeal, rejected the same outright' by his Order bearing Nothi No.4 A(9) 116/Mushak/ Appeal/2006/1213 dated 5-10-2006. Against this Order the petitioner filed Appeal to respondent No.1. Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as the Appellate Tribunal) on 6-10-2006 with the prayer for accepting the Appeal for hearing by waiving deposit of 25% of the demanded or imposed penalty under Section 42 of the VAT Act read with Section 196 and 2nd proviso to section 194 of the Customs Act. At the time of hearing of the Appeal on 5-2-2007, the petitioner filed an application to accept the Memo of Appeal by waiving deposit of 25% of the demanded VAT or imposed penalty. The petitioner also submit- ted a certificate issued by Janata Bank, Local Office, Dilkusha Commercial Area, Dhaka under Nothi No. Lo/ICD/JMS GLASS/07 dated 31-1-2007 showing its bank liability to the tune, of Taka 79,14,280.68. The petitioner also brought to the attention of the respondent of the observations made by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 3207 of 2003 and 3028 of 2003 as to the jurisdiction in the matter of accepting Appeal pending deposit. A copy of the interim Order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 11234 of 2006 relating to CEVTI case No. 59/2006 was also submitted. But respondent No. 1 without exercising his power tinder the said provisions' of the VAT Act read with the Customs Act and considering the observations made by the High Court Division in the above mentioned writ petitions and interim Order passed in similar cases denied proper dispensation of justice to the petitioner by asking it to deposit VAT as per the VAT Act and submit the treasury chalan of such deposit before the Tribunal by 18-4-2007 vide Nothi No. CEVT/case (VAT) 192120061667(1) dated 15-3-2007. And being aggrieved by the Order of respondent No. 1, the petitioner filed the writ petition.

4. No affidavit-in-opposition was filed by the writ-respondents before the High Court Division. However, Mrs Sathika Hossain, learned Assistant Attorney General, appeared for the writ-respondents and made verbal submissions. A Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing the writ petition along with other writ petitions involving similar question of law by the impugned judgment and Order discharged the Rule.

5. Mrs Nahid Mahtab, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner has contended that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in deciding the merit of the instant Rule relying on the decision given by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 576 of 2005 inasmuch as the facts and circumstances of the said case have got no bearing in the context of the present case; in the earlier case the point raised was whether an Appeal filed without deposit would be deemed to have 'been allowed after expiry of the statutory period, whereas the point in the present case was whether the Appellate Tribunal had got the authority to consider an application for waiving/dispensing deposit of the demanded VAT or the penalty Imposed. She has further contended that if the second proviso to section 194 of the Customs Act is read together with the provisions of section 42(1) (Ka) (Kha) of the Act, it would appear that the Appellate Tribunal has jurisdiction to waive/dispense with the deposit of the demanded VAT or imposed penalty, but the learned Judges of the High Court Division on wrong interpretation of the said provisions of the VAT Act and Customs Act held that the Tribunal had no jurisdiction to waive deposit of 25% of the demanded VAT or penalty for accepting an Appeal as required under the provisions of section 42(2)(ga) of the VAT Act and thus erred in law in discharging the Rule. She has lastly contended that leave may be granted to decide the point finally as to whether the Appellate Tribunal can accept the Appeal filed before it by waiving/dispensing with the deposit as mandated in clause (ga) of sub-section (2) of section 42 of the VAT Act in view of the provisions of clause (Kha) of sub-section (1) (Ka) thereof read with the second proviso to section 194 of the Customs Act.

6. From the facts as stated in the writ petition as well as in the leave petition, it is clear that the Appeal filed by the petitioner before the Commissioner (Appeal) against the Order of adjudication passed by the Assistant Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT was rejected on the ground that it did not deposit the demanded VAT or 10% of the penalty in the Government treasury pursuant to see tins 42 (Ka) of the VAT Act. And then against the sold Order of the Commissioner (Appeal), the petitioner filed an Appeal before the Appellate Tribunal Dhaka. And again without making any statutory; deposit as provided in section 42(2)(ga) of the VAT Act. However, the petitioner filed an application before the Appellate Tribunal to hear the Appeal it? out making the statutory by it invoking the pro- visions of second proviso to section 194 read with section 196 of the Customs Act. The Tribunal did not concede to the prayer of the petitioner and asked it to make the statutory and submit treasury chalan by 18-4-2007. The petitioner without complying with the Order of the Tribunal filed the writ petition and obtained the Rule.

7. From the impugned judgment and Order, it appears that the High Court Division considering the provisions of section 42 (2) of the VAT Act as it stood in 1995 and the subsequent amendment of the said section vide Finance Act, 1996 by which clauses (Ka) and (Kha) were inserted in sub-section (2) of section 42 and the second proviso to section 194 of the Customs Act came to the clear finding that the Tribunal had no jurisdiction to waive/dispose "with the mandatory requirement of deposit of a percent- age of demanded VAT or penalty to entertain an Appeal in a case under VAT Act following the pro- vision of second proviso to section 194 (1) of the Customs Act". In taking the above view, the Tribunal relied upon an unreported judgment passed in Writ Petition No. 6895 of 1997, the name of the parties being Asif Steels Limited vs The Commissioner of Customs, Customs House, Chittagong and others and the judgment passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 576 of 2005. Accordingly, the learned Judges did not find any illegality with the impugned letter issued from the office of the Appellate Tribunal.

8. In view of the submissions made by Mrs Nahid Mahtab and the finding of the High Court Division the only question to be decided in this petition for leave to Appeal is as to whether the Appellate Tribunal had any jurisdiction to consider the prayer of the petitioner to waive/dispense with the statutory deposit as mandated in section 42 (2) (ga) of the VAT Act by applying the provisions of second proviso to section 194 of the Customs Act in view of the provisions of clause (Kha) of sub sec don (1) (Ka) of section 42 of the VAT Act and whether the Appellate Tribunal was justified in directing the petitioner to deposit the demanded VAT as per the VAT Act in the proper head and submit the treasury chalan by 17-4-2007.

9. For our present sub-section 42 of the VAT Act is relevant and accordingly, subsection (2) of the section is quoted herein below:- ৪২। আপীল। (২) যদি কোন ব্যক্তি কোনো পণ্য বা সেবার উপর প্রদেয় মূল্য সংযোজন করের দাবী সম্পর্কিত অথবা এই আইনের অধীন আরোপিত কোনো অর্থদন্ড সম্পর্কিত কোনো সিদ্ধান্ত বা আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন আপীল করার ইচ্ছা করেন, তাহা হইলে তাহাকে, তাহার আপীল দায়ের করার কালে আপীলটি-

(ক) কমিশনার (আপীল) এর নিকট দায়ের করা হইলে, দাবীকৃত কর বা আরোপিত অর্থদন্ডের দশ শতাংশ,

(খ) কমিশনার বা তাহার সমমর্যাদার কোনো মূল্য সংযোজন কর্মকর্তার আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে Appellate Tribunal এ দায়ের করা হইলে, দাবীকৃত কর বা আরোপিত অর্থদন্ডের পঁচিশ শতাংশ, এবং

(গ) কমিশনার (আপীল) এর আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে Appellate Tribunal এ দায়ের করা হইলে, দাবীকৃত কর বা আরোপিত অর্থদন্ডের পনের শতাংশ সরকারীতে ট্রেজারী বা সরকারের নিকট হইতে এতদুদ্দেশ্যে ক্ষমতাপ্রাপ্ত কোনো মূল্য সংযোজন কর কর্মকর্তার নিকট জমা করিতে হইবে।

10. From a close reading of clauses (Ka) and (ga) of sub-section (2) of section 42 of the VAT Act, it appears that it is a precondition to make deposit of 10% of the demanded VAT or penalty imposed to file an Appeal before the Commissioner (Appeal) and to deposit 15% of the demanded VAT or penalty imposed to file an Appeal before the Appellate Tribunal respectively. The said two clauses further show that no power or authority has been given either to the Commissioner (Appeal) or to the Appellate Tribunal to waive or dispense with the deposit of the VAT or imposed penalty as mandated therein.

11. In the instant case, two Appeals are involved, one before the Commissioner (Appeal) and the other before the Appellate Tribunal. So far as the Appeal before the Commissioner (Appeal) is concerned no reference whatsoever has been made to the Customs Act. And in clause (Ka) of sub-section 1 (Ka) of section 42 of the VAT Act detailed procedure has been made as to how the Commissioner (Appeal) shall dispose of the Appeal and also the nature of Order he would be able to pass. So, with the memorandum of Appeal, the petitioner was obliged to deposit 10% of the demanded VAT or the imposed penalty as per provisions of clause (Ka) of sub-section (2) of section 42 of the VAT Act and without such deposit the Appeal before Commissioner (Appeal) was incompetent. So far as the Appeal before the Appellate Tribunal is concerned, it has been provided in clause (Kha) of sub-section (1) (Ka) of section 42 of the Act that the same shall be disposed of as far as practicable following the provisions of Customs Act regarding the Tribunal under the Customs Act irrespective of the provisions made in the VAT Act.

12. Now the pertinent question is whether an Appeal filed before the Appellate Tribunal without making the statutory deposit as mandated in clause (ga) of sub-section (2) of section 42 of the VAT Act can be treated or accepted as an Appeal in the eye of law. The VAT Act and the Customs Act are two separate statutes and one statute cannot overlap the pro- visions of the other statute unless any specific reference is made in the respective statutes itself about overlapping as has been in respect of the disposal of the Appeal filed under the VAT Act by clause (Kha) of sub-section 1 (Ka) of section 42 of the VAT Act as mentioned hereinbefore.

13. In section 193 of the Customs Act, specific provisions have been made for filing an Appeal to the Commissioner (Appeal within the time as mentioned therein if any person feels aggrieved by any decision or Order passed under the Customs Act, not being a decision or Order passed under section 82 or section 98 thereof by an officer of Customs lower in rank than a Commissioner of Customs including the power to extend the period up to a further period of 2 (two) months. In section 193, detail procedure has been laid down as to how an Appeal filed under the section shall be disposed of by the Commissioner (Appeal). Section 196 of the Customs Act has spelt out that the Government shall constitute an Appellate Tribunal to be called the Customs, Excise and মূল্য সংযোজন কর Appellate Tribunal which shall consist of as many technical and judicial members as it thinks fit to exercise the power and discharge the functions conferred on the Appellate Tribunal by the Act. In the section, it has also been provided what shall be the qualification of a technical member and a judicial member and who shall be the president of the Tribunal.
